1.179.s:
1.211
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
dṛṣṭvā gandharvarājasya krodhenākulitaṃ manaḥ ..
tamūcurnṛpa gandharvāḥ svabāhubaladarpitāḥ .. 1 ..
1.179.d:
1.211
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
दृष्ट्वा गन्धर्वराजस्य क्रोधेनाकुलितं मनः ॥
तमूचुर्नृप गन्धर्वाः स्वबाहुबलदर्पिताः ॥ 1 ॥
1.179.m:
1.211
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Seeing the mind of the Gandharva king disturbed with anger,
the Gandharvas, proud of the strength of their own arms, said to him, O king:

1.179.s:
aparājita uvāca ..
sarvamālabhate rājannaśokaḥ śūrabāhuṣu ..
tasmācchauryeṇa nidhanaṃ raghūṇāṃ mama rocate .. 2 ..
1.179.d:
अपराजित उवाच ॥
सर्वमालभते राजन्नशोकः शूरबाहुषु ॥
तस्माच्छौर्येण निधनं रघूणां मम रोचते ॥ 2 ॥

1.179.s:
nikumbha uvāca ..
yo'yaṃ manyuḥ samudbhūtaḥ kākutsthānprati me prabho ..
avināśi jagatkṛtsnaṃ vināśaṃ samupaiṣyati .. 3 ..
1.179.d:
निकुम्भ उवाच ॥
योऽयं मन्युः समुद्भूतः काकुत्स्थान्प्रति मे प्रभो ॥
अविनाशि जगत्कृत्स्नं विनाशं समुपैष्यति ॥ 3 ॥
1.179.m:
Nikumbha said:
O lord, through this fury that has arisen in me against the descendants of Kakutstha,
the entire indestructible world will meet with destruction.

1.179.s:
.. kinnara uvāca ..
yā lakṣmīranuliptāṅgī vairiśoṇitakuṅkumaiḥ..
kāntāpi sarasāṃ prītiṃ na sā dhatte manasvinām.. 4 ..
1.179.d:
॥ किन्नर उवाच ॥
या लक्ष्मीरनुलिप्ताङ्गी वैरिशोणितकुङ्कुमैः॥
कान्तापि सरसां प्रीतिं न सा धत्ते मनस्विनाम्॥ 4 ॥
1.179.m:
Kinnara said:
That fortune whose limbs are anointed with saffron of enemies' blood,
even if beloved, does not give juicy delight to high-minded men [unless won in battle].

1.179.s:
vasunābha uvāca ..
kṛpāṇadhārāvidhvastaśatrusaṅghasamudbhavā ..
na yā śrīḥ kiṃ tayā kāryaṃ rājansattvavatāṃ nṛṇām .. 5 ..
1.179.d:
वसुनाभ उवाच ॥
कृपाणधाराविध्वस्तशत्रुसङ्घसमुद्भवा ॥
न या श्रीः किं तया कार्यं राजन्सत्त्ववतां नृणाम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.179.m:
Vasunābha said:
O king, what use is that fortune to resolute men
which does not arise from destroying hosts of enemies with the edge of the sword?

1.179.s:
.. ajagara uvāca ..
ajitārigaṇopāntasampado bhūṣaṇakriyā ..
vipadvarīyasī tābhiryā na sampadvibhūṣaṇā .. 6 ..
1.179.d:
॥ अजगर उवाच ॥
अजितारिगणोपान्तसम्पदो भूषणक्रिया ॥
विपद्वरीयसी ताभिर्या न सम्पद्विभूषणा ॥ 6 ॥

1.179.s:
.. ruha uvāca ..
śobhante karkaśāḥ śūrāḥ stanā iva samunnatāḥ ..
śūrāṇāṃ ca stanānāṃ ca parāvajñākarī ratiḥ .. 7 ..
1.179.d:
॥ रुह उवाच ॥
शोभन्ते कर्कशाः शूराः स्तना इव समुन्नताः ॥
शूराणां च स्तनानां च परावज्ञाकरी रतिः ॥ 7 ॥

1.179.s:
..keśa uvāca ..
tejasvināmabhyudayaṃ vandanīyaṃ jagattraye ..
yathā bhāskaramudyantaṃ janaḥ sarvo'bhinandati .. 8 ..
1.179.d:
॥केश उवाच ॥
तेजस्विनामभ्युदयं वन्दनीयं जगत्त्रये ॥
यथा भास्करमुद्यन्तं जनः सर्वोऽभिनन्दति ॥ 8 ॥
1.179.m:
Keśa said:
The rise of the radiant is to be saluted in the three worlds,
just as everyone rejoices at the rising sun.

1.179.s:
.. paravāraṇa uvāca ..
sattvādhikasya siṃhasya līlonmathitapādapāḥ ..
na śaktāḥ purataḥ sthātuṃ śailakūṭopamā gajāḥ .. 9 ..
1.179.d:
॥ परवारण उवाच ॥
सत्त्वाधिकस्य सिंहस्य लीलोन्मथितपादपाः ॥
न शक्ताः पुरतः स्थातुं शैलकूटोपमा गजाः ॥ 9 ॥
1.179.m:
Paravāraṇa said:
Elephants resembling mountain peaks, who playfully crush trees,
are not able to stand before a lion of superior courage.

1.179.s:
.. ābhāvaha uvāca ..
na jātu śamanaṃ yasya tejastejasi tejasām ..
vṛthā jātena kiṃ tena māturvārddhakya kāriṇā .. 1.211.10 ..
1.179.d:
॥ आभावह उवाच ॥
न जातु शमनं यस्य तेजस्तेजसि तेजसाम् ॥
वृथा जातेन किं तेन मातुर्वार्द्धक्य कारिणा ॥ 1.211.10 ॥
1.179.m:
Ābhāvaha said:
He whose fiery energy never suppresses the energy of the energetic—
what is the use of him being born in vain, merely causing old age to his mother?

1.179.s:
ekalavya uvāca ..
nāmni saṃkīrtite yasya na bhavantyarayo bhayāt ..
vivarṇavadanacchāyāḥ kā dayā tasya jīvane .. 11 ..
1.179.d:
एकलव्य उवाच ॥
नाम्नि संकीर्तिते यस्य न भवन्त्यरयो भयात् ॥
विवर्णवदनच्छायाः का दया तस्य जीवने ॥ 11 ॥
1.179.m:
Ekalavya said:
He when whose name is proclaimed the enemies do not out of fear
become pale-complexioned in their faces—what pity is there for his life?

1.179.s:
viśāla uvāca ..
lakṣmīsaṅgamalubdhānāṃ śūrāṇāṃ ca raṇodbhavā ..
kīrtirbhavati saivāśu saṃyogakaraṇā sakhī .. 12 ..
1.179.d:
विशाल उवाच ॥
लक्ष्मीसङ्गमलुब्धानां शूराणां च रणोद्भवा ॥
कीर्तिर्भवति सैवाशु संयोगकरणा सखी ॥ 12 ॥
1.179.m:
Viśāla said:
For heroes eager to unite with royal fortune and born of battle,
fame immediately becomes the friend that arranges that union.

1.179.s:
.. kalipriya uvāca ..
ripuraktaparā siktā ripustrīnetravāriṇā ..
na yasya siñcitā kīrtiḥ kā spṛhā tasya jīvane .. 13 ..
1.179.d:
॥ कलिप्रिय उवाच ॥
रिपुरक्तपरा सिक्ता रिपुस्त्रीनेत्रवारिणा ॥
न यस्य सिञ्चिता कीर्तिः का स्पृहा तस्य जीवने ॥ 13 ॥
1.179.m:
Kalipriya said:
He whose fame, moist with enemy blood, is not further
sprinkled by the tears of enemies' women—what longing can he have for life?

1.179.s:
.. bhīmanāda uvāca ..
tejasaiva samākrāntasamastabhuvano raviḥ ..
karoti padavinyāsaṃ sarveṣāmeva mūrdhasu .. 14 ..
1.179.d:
॥ भीमनाद उवाच ॥
तेजसैव समाक्रान्तसमस्तभुवनो रविः ॥
करोति पदविन्यासं सर्वेषामेव मूर्धसु ॥ 14 ॥
1.179.m:
Bhīmanāda said:
The sun, having pervaded all the worlds with its splendor alone,
places its footsteps upon the heads of all.

1.179.s:
..mahādharma uvāca ..
śatrumastakavinyastapadakramavilāsinī ..
kavidattakarālambā kīrtiryātu divaṃ tava .. 15 ..
1.179.d:
॥महाधर्म उवाच ॥
शत्रुमस्तकविन्यस्तपदक्रमविलासिनी ॥
कविदत्तकरालम्बा कीर्तिर्यातु दिवं तव ॥ 15 ॥
1.179.m:
Mahādharma said:
Delighting in placing its steps on the heads of enemies,
supported by the hand given by a poet, may your fame go to heaven.

1.179.s:
.. vāsukiruvāca ..
māyānihatamātaṅgamadhyadvīpavidāritām ..
kṣitiṃ bhittvāviśatkanyā kīrtito vasudhātalam .. 16..
1.179.d:
॥ वासुकिरुवाच ॥
मायानिहतमातङ्गमध्यद्वीपविदारिताम् ॥
क्षितिं भित्त्वाविशत्कन्या कीर्तितो वसुधातलम् ॥ 16॥
1.179.m:
Vāsuki said:
Splitting the earth torn in the middle island where elephants were slain by magical illusion,
the maiden of your fame has entered the surface of the earth.

1.179.s:
.. panasa uvāca ..
hatārilakṣmīsaṃyogavikasadvadanasya te ..
prayātu tvaritā kīrtiḥ krodhaneva diśo daśa ..17..
1.179.d:
॥ पनस उवाच ॥
हतारिलक्ष्मीसंयोगविकसद्वदनस्य ते ॥
प्रयातु त्वरिता कीर्तिः क्रोधनेव दिशो दश ॥17॥
1.179.m:
Panasa said:
May your fame, swift as if angry,
go to the ten directions for you whose face blossoms from union with the fortune of slain enemies.

1.179.s:
gada uvāca...
satoyatoyadākārairnāgairdānapravarṣibhiḥ ..
ākrāntadiṅmukhe yuddhe vidyuttvamme karotvasiḥ .. 18 ..
1.179.d:
गद उवाच॥।
सतोयतोयदाकारैर्नागैर्दानप्रवर्षिभिः ॥
आक्रान्तदिङ्मुखे युद्धे विद्युत्त्वम्मे करोत्वसिः ॥ 18 ॥
1.179.m:
Gada said:
In battle where the faces of the directions are overtaken by elephants like rain clouds pouring rut-fluid,
let my sword act as lightning.

1.179.s:
mahānāda uvāca ..
madīyasiṃhanādena vitrāsitagajākulam ..
balaṃ nipātayārīṇāṃ śaraiḥ sannataparvabhiḥ .. 19 ..
1.179.d:
महानाद उवाच ॥
मदीयसिंहनादेन वित्रासितगजाकुलम् ॥
बलं निपातयारीणां शरैः सन्नतपर्वभिः ॥ 19 ॥
1.179.m:
Mahānāda said:
Cast down with arrows of straight joints the army of the enemies,
which is agitated with elephants terrified by my lion-roar.

1.179.s:
vasuruvāca ..
gajāśvarathapādātacaraṇollikhitaṃ rajaḥ ..
draṣṭāsi praśamaṃ yātaṃ paritastvariśoṇitaiḥ .. 1.211.20 ..
1.179.d:
वसुरुवाच ॥
गजाश्वरथपादातचरणोल्लिखितं रजः ॥
द्रष्टासि प्रशमं यातं परितस्त्वरिशोणितैः ॥ 1.211.20 ॥
1.179.m:
Vasu said:
You will see the dust kicked up by the feet of elephants, horses, chariots, and foot-soldiers
quickly completely settled by the blood of enemies.

1.179.s:
vṛndāraka uvāca ..
gajakumbhasamudrasthamuktāphalavikāsiṣu ..
tiṣṭhatsu rājankhaḍgeṣu kaḥ saheta parābhavam .. 21 ..
1.179.d:
वृन्दारक उवाच ॥
गजकुम्भसमुद्रस्थमुक्ताफलविकासिषु ॥
तिष्ठत्सु राजन्खड्गेषु कः सहेत पराभवम् ॥ 21 ॥
1.179.m:
Vṛndāraka said:
While swords stand shining with pearls from the ocean of elephants' frontal globes,
O king, who would tolerate defeat?

1.179.s:
.. jyotiṣika uvāca ..
kāpiśabhrūlatābhaṅgakuṭiladvayakoṭiṣu ..
vidyamāneṣu cāpeṣu kaḥ saheta parābhavam .. 22 ..
1.179.d:
॥ ज्योतिषिक उवाच ॥
कापिशभ्रूलताभङ्गकुटिलद्वयकोटिषु ॥
विद्यमानेषु चापेषु कः सहेत पराभवम् ॥ 22 ॥
1.179.m:
Jyotiṣika said:
While bows exist whose two ends are curved like the bending of brown creepers of eyebrows,
who would tolerate defeat?

1.179.s:
dṛḍhasyuruvāca ..
rājaṃstīkṣṇāḥ santi yasya viśikhāḥ pañca māninaḥ ..
kimanyaistasya kartavyaṃ pakṣapātibhirāhave .. 23 ..
1.179.d:
दृढस्युरुवाच ॥
राजंस्तीक्ष्णाः सन्ति यस्य विशिखाः पञ्च मानिनः ॥
किमन्यैस्तस्य कर्तव्यं पक्षपातिभिराहवे ॥ 23 ॥
1.179.m:
Dṛḍhasyu said:
O king, for a proud man who has five sharp arrows,
what need is there of others who take sides in battle?

1.179.s:
candrāpīḍa uvāca ..
kimāyudhaiḥ sattvavatāṃ cārudordaṇḍa śālinām ..
sadyaḥ sañjātamanyūnāṃ yuddhavyākṣepakārakaiḥ .. 24 ..
1.179.d:
चन्द्रापीड उवाच ॥
किमायुधैः सत्त्ववतां चारुदोर्दण्ड शालिनाम् ॥
सद्यः सञ्जातमन्यूनां युद्धव्याक्षेपकारकैः ॥ 24 ॥
1.179.m:
Candrāpīḍa said:
What need is there of weapons that delay the fight
for resolute men possessing beautiful staff-like arms, whose fury has just arisen?

1.179.s:
gadyuruvāca ..
khaḍgāstiṣṭhantu me tucchā bhuktabhaṅgāṭṭahāsinaḥ ..
ekadordaṇḍaśeṣo'pi kaḥ saheta parābhavam .. 25 ..
1.179.d:
गद्युरुवाच ॥
खड्गास्तिष्ठन्तु मे तुच्छा भुक्तभङ्गाट्टहासिनः ॥
एकदोर्दण्डशेषोऽपि कः सहेत पराभवम् ॥ 25 ॥

1.179.s:
kalaviṅka uvāca ..
madbāhumandarakṣubdhavairisainyamahārṇavāt ..
bhuṅkṣva lakṣmīṃ samutpannāṃ cirāya jagatīpate .. 26 ..
1.179.d:
कलविङ्क उवाच ॥
मद्बाहुमन्दरक्षुब्धवैरिसैन्यमहार्णवात् ॥
भुङ्क्ष्व लक्ष्मीं समुत्पन्नां चिराय जगतीपते ॥ 26 ॥
1.179.m:
Kalaviṅka said:
Enjoy for a long time, O ruler of the earth, the fortune produced
from the great ocean of the enemy army churned by my arm like Mount Mandara.

1.179.s:
.. gaja uvāca ..
kimāyudhaiḥ sattvavatāṃ kupuṃsāṃ ca kimāyudhaiḥ ..
arātiśastrāṇyekeṣāmanyeṣāmaphalāni hi .. 27 ..
1.179.d:
॥ गज उवाच ॥
किमायुधैः सत्त्ववतां कुपुंसां च किमायुधैः ॥
अरातिशस्त्राण्येकेषामन्येषामफलानि हि ॥ 27 ॥
1.179.m:
Gaja said:
What use are weapons to resolute men, and what use are weapons to cowards?
To the former, the weapons of enemies [are enough]; to the latter, indeed, they are useless.

1.179.s:
balaka uvāca ..
durbalotkhāta śakrebhadaśanābhihate harau ..
mayādya surarāḍastu bhavāṃstribhuvaneśvaraḥ .. 28 .. ..
1.179.d:
बलक उवाच ॥
दुर्बलोत्खात शक्रेभदशनाभिहते हरौ ॥
मयाद्य सुरराडस्तु भवांस्त्रिभुवनेश्वरः ॥ 28 ॥ ॥
1.179.m:
Balaka said:
When Śakra's elephant has its tusks torn out by the weak, and Hari is struck down,
may you become the king of the gods today, and ruler of the three worlds.

1.179.s:
pranaṣṭadevatāpūjaṃ balihīnaṃ sudurdaśam ..
mayā kṛtamathādyāstu trailokyamapi suprabho .. 29 ..
1.179.d:
प्रनष्टदेवतापूजं बलिहीनं सुदुर्दशम् ॥
मया कृतमथाद्यास्तु त्रैलोक्यमपि सुप्रभो ॥ 29 ॥
1.179.m:
O radiant lord, let even the three worlds be made by me today
free of worship to gods, devoid of offerings, and reduced to a wretched state.

1.179.s:
harika uvāca ..
kīnāśamahiṣeṇādya harasya vṛṣabheṇa tu ..
ayodhyāṃ vāhayiṣyāmi śeṣāherlāṅgalena ca .. 1.211.30 ..
1.179.d:
हरिक उवाच ॥
कीनाशमहिषेणाद्य हरस्य वृषभेण तु ॥
अयोध्यां वाहयिष्यामि शेषाहेर्लाङ्गलेन च ॥ 1.211.30 ॥
1.179.m:
Harika said:
Today, with the buffalo of Yama and the bull of Hara,
and with the serpent Śeṣa as a plow, I will cultivate Ayodhyā.

1.179.s:
mahodara uvāca ..
nirastamayamārtaṇḍe mayā loke carācare ..
yamasya mahiṣaṃ paśya kramantaṃ sūryavājiṣu .. 31 ..
1.179.d:
महोदर उवाच ॥
निरस्तमयमार्तण्डे मया लोके चराचरे ॥
यमस्य महिषं पश्य क्रमन्तं सूर्यवाजिषु ॥ 31 ॥
1.179.m:
Mahodara said:
When the moving and unmoving world has had its sun cast into night by me,
behold the buffalo of Yama trampling the horses of the sun.

1.179.s:
sūrya uvāca ..
niḥśeṣadevatāsaṃghe mayā lokatraye kṛte ..
durgāsiṃhavinirbhinnaṃ paśyādya maghavadgajam .. 32 ..
1.179.d:
सूर्य उवाच ॥
निःशेषदेवतासंघे मया लोकत्रये कृते ॥
दुर्गासिंहविनिर्भिन्नं पश्याद्य मघवद्गजम् ॥ 32 ॥
1.179.m:
Sūrya said:
When the three worlds have been emptied by me of all hosts of deities,
behold today the elephant of Indra torn apart by the lion of Durgā.

1.179.s:
prabhasa uvāca ..
nirastāmbupipāsena samākṛṣṭa dhaneśvarāḥ ..
praṇamantu tavādyaiva devasaṃghā hatatviṣaḥ .. 33 ..
1.179.d:
प्रभस उवाच ॥
निरस्ताम्बुपिपासेन समाकृष्ट धनेश्वराः ॥
प्रणमन्तु तवाद्यैव देवसंघा हतत्विषः ॥ 33 ॥
1.179.m:
Prabhasa said:
Drawn out by me, whose thirst for water is quenched, let the hosts of gods, their radiance destroyed, / bow before you this very day, O lord of wealth!

1.179.s:
bhadraka uvāca ..
skandaśaṅkaraśūnye'sminmayā tribhuvane kṛte ..

1.179.d:
भद्रक उवाच ॥
स्कन्दशङ्करशून्येऽस्मिन्मया त्रिभुवने कृते ॥
शिखी संभक्षयत्वद्य शर्वाभरणपन्नगान् ॥ 34 ॥
1.179.m:
Bhadraka said:
When I have emptied these three worlds of Skanda and Śaṅkara, / let the peacock eat Śarva's ornament-snakes today!

1.179.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
क्रोधान्धकारकलुषीकृतचारुवक्त्रान्गन्धर्वराजतनयान्प्रसमीक्षमाणः ॥
जगाद राजानमदीन सत्त्वो नाडायनाख्यस्तु तदा पुरोधाः ॥ 35 ॥
1.212
॥ नाडायन उवाच ॥ ॥
एकया द्वे विनिश्चित्य त्रींश्चतुर्भिर्वशीकुरु ॥
पञ्च जित्वा विजित्वा षट् सप्त हित्वा सुखी भव ॥ 1 ॥
एकया प्रज्ञया राजन्कार्याकार्यद्वयं नरः ॥
विनिश्चित्य तु यः कुर्यात्कार्यं तत्र स पण्डितः ॥ 2 ॥
मध्यस्थं यदि वा मित्रं शत्रुं वा कार्यगौरवात् ॥
ज्ञात्वा देशं च कालं च ह्युपायैरभ्युपक्रमेत् ॥ 3 ॥
सामभेदप्रदानाश्च उपायाः परिकीर्तिताः ॥
उपायश्च चतुर्थो ऽत्र दण्डस्त्वगतिका गतिः ॥ 4 ॥
पञ्चेन्द्रियजयो येन कृत आदौ जिगीषुणा ॥
त्रिलोकविजयं तस्य न दूरे प्रतिभाति मे ॥ 5 ॥
पञ्चेन्द्रिय जयं कृत्वा गुणषट्कमुपाश्रयेत् ॥
बुद्ध्वा बलाबलं सम्यगात्मनश्चापरस्य च ॥ 6 ॥
1.179.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Seeing the sons of the king of the Gandharvas, their handsome faces darkened by the gloom of rage, / the royal priest named Nāḍāyana, whose spirit was undaunted, then spoke to the king:
1.212
Nāḍāyana said:
Determining the two through the one, master the three through the four; / conquering the five and overcoming the six, abandoning the seven, be happy!
By means of the one discernment, O king, a man determines the two—what should and should not be done; / and he who performs what should be done is a wise man in this regard.
Whether one be neutral, a friend, or an enemy, because of the gravity of the task, / having considered both place and time, one should proceed by means of the [four] expedients.
Conciliation, sowing dissension, and gift are declared as the expedients; / and the fourth expedient here, force, is the recourse when there is no other recourse.
By him who, desiring victory, has first conquered the five senses, / the conquest of the three worlds, it seems to me, is not far off.
Having achieved the conquest of the five senses, one should resort to the six royal policies, / having correctly understood the strengths and weaknesses of both oneself and the other.

1.179.d:
राजदोषाः परित्यक्ता येन सप्त नराधिप ॥
सिद्धिं तस्य समायान्ति यथाकालं गुणा नृप ॥ 7 ॥
मृगयायानमुख्याश्च स्त्रियश्च पुरुषा गिरः ॥
अर्थसन्दूषणं चैव दण्डपारुष्यमेव च ॥ 8 ॥
राजदोषैः परित्यक्ता राघवास्तत्र पार्थिव ॥
गुणाश्रयविभागज्ञा विग्रहस्तैर्न रोचते ॥ 9 ॥
भरतेन वयं साम्ना बले महति तिष्ठता ॥
प्रथमं समुपाक्रान्तं तदेव तव रोचताम् ॥ 1.212.10 ॥
भरतस्य वयं साम्ना यदि गच्छेम पर्वतम् ॥
हितं तत्स्यान्महाभाग सकुलस्य तवाऽनघ ॥ 11 ॥
त्वया कृत्वा समुच्छेदं राज्ञां जननिवासिनाम् ॥
अकारणान्महद्वैरं कृतं भूपतिभिः सह ॥ 12 ॥
जने निवासादस्माकं केवलं लघुता भवेत् ॥
मानुषैः संगमश्चैव विग्रहश्च पुनःपुनः ॥ 13 ॥
1.179.m:
By whom the seven royal vices have been abandoned, O lord of men, / to him accomplishments come in due time, O king.
Hunting, travel [or gambling], women, harsh words, / squandering of wealth, and harshness of punishment—
the descendants of Raghu, O earth-ruler, are free from these royal vices; / knowing the proper classification of the six policies, conflict with them is not advisable.
We were first approached peacefully by Bharata, who possesses a vast army; / let that very [peace] be pleasing to you.
If we were to go to the mountain peacefully with Bharata, / that would be beneficial, O illustrious and sinless one, to you along with your kin.
By bringing about the destruction of the kings who dwell among the people, / you have made great enmity with the rulers of the earth without cause.
From living among humans, only diminishment would be ours, / as well as contact and repeated conflict with mortals.

1.179.d:
न कृषिर्न च वाणिज्यं जनोऽस्माकं प्रयोजनम् ॥
ते वयं सजनां भूमिं त्यक्त्वा यामः शिलोच्चयम् ॥ 14 ॥
अपेक्ष्य देशकालौ च संधिं विग्रहमेव च ॥
फलं च बुद्ध्वा यः कुर्यात्स राजन्पण्डितो नरः ॥ 15 ॥
भूमिर्हिरण्यं मित्रं च त्रिविधं विग्रहास्पदम् ॥
स्वयंग्राहो यदस्माकं मेरुः कनकपर्वतः ॥ ॥ 16 ॥
हिरण्येन तदा कार्यं न नोऽस्ति रिपुसूदन ॥
कृषिर्नास्ति यतोऽस्माकं ततो भूर्निष्प्रयोजना ॥ 17 ॥
तस्माद्भरतमन्विच्छ मित्रं साम्ना नराधिप ॥
मित्रं रघुकुलं कृत्वा निवासस्तु हिमाचले ॥ 18 ॥
अदृश्यं देवसैन्यानां सुखं चिरमवाप्नुहि ॥
न मानुषोऽयमित्येवं भरतं मन्तुमर्हसि ॥ 19 ॥
दुष्टानां निग्रहार्थाय चतुर्मूर्तिर्जनार्दनः ॥
जातो रघुकुले राजन्पुत्रो दशरथस्य तु ॥1.212.20॥
1.179.m:
Neither agriculture nor trade among the people is our concern; / let us abandon this inhabited land and go to the mountain.
Considering place and time, peace and war, / and discerning the result, he who acts, O king, is a wise man.
Land, gold, and an ally are the threefold grounds of conflict; / whereas our own possession is Meru, the golden mountain.
Then, O slayer of foes, we have no need for gold; / since we have no agriculture, land is of no use to us.
Therefore, O ruler of men, seek out Bharata as an ally through conciliation; / having made the family of Raghu an ally, our dwelling shall be on the Himācala.
Unseen by divine armies, enjoy happiness for a long time! / You should not consider Bharata as merely human.
For the restraint of the wicked, Janārdana of four forms / was born in the family of Raghu, O king, as the son of Daśaratha.

1.179.d:
अंशेन वासुदेवस्य जातो रामो महायशाः ॥
संकर्षणस्य चांशेन लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा ॥ 21 ॥
प्रद्युम्नस्य तथांशेन भरतो धर्मवत्सलः ॥
अनिरुद्धस्य चांशेन शत्रुघ्नः सुमहाबलः ॥ ॥ 22 ॥
तत्र राघवसिंहेन रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा ॥
रावणोऽभिहतः संख्ये सर्वसत्त्वभयङ्करः ॥ 23 ॥
मेघनादो निरस्तश्च संग्रामे लक्ष्मणेन च ॥
शत्रुघ्नेन निरस्तश्च लवणो दुष्टराक्षसः ॥ 24 ॥
मन्ये विशिष्टभावत्वं भरतस्य महात्मनः ॥
येन माली हतः पूर्वं लङ्कावासी स राक्षसः ॥ 25 ॥
स एष भरतो विष्णुरस्ति ते तु रणंगमः॥26॥
हिते स्थितो यः सततं सुराणां दैत्येन्द्रनाशाय निविष्टबुद्धिः ॥
तेनाऽप्रमेयेण जनार्दनेन समं व्रजस्वाशु महानुभाव ॥ 27 ॥
1.179.m:
As a portion of Vāsudeva, the renowned Rāma was born; / and as a portion of Saṃkarṣaṇa, Lakṣmaṇa, the slayer of enemy warriors.
Likewise, as a portion of Pradyumna, Bharata, who loves dharma, was born; / and as a portion of Aniruddha, Śatrughna of immense strength.
There, by Rāma, the lion of the Raghus, whose deeds are effortless, / Rāvaṇa, who caused terror to all living beings, was slain in battle.
Meghanāda was cast down in battle by Lakṣmaṇa, / and by Śatrughna, the wicked rākṣasa Lavaṇa was destroyed.
I consider the nature of the great-souled Bharata to be superior, / by whom previously Mālī, that rākṣasa dwelling in Laṅkā, was slain.
This Bharata is Viṣṇu, who is marching to battle against you.
Who constantly abides in the welfare of the gods, his mind resolved upon the destruction of the lords of the Daityas— / make peace swiftly, O illustrious one, with that immeasurable Janārdana!

1.179.d:
1.213
॥ शैलूष उवाच ॥
सुमाली विष्णुना पूर्वं कथं युद्धे निपातितः ॥
एतन्मे संशयं छिन्धि श्रूयते स महाबलः ॥ 1 ॥
नाडायन उवाच ॥
कथेयं राजशार्दूल पुरागस्त्येन धीमता ॥
रामाय कथिता वीर तां मे निगदतः शृणु ॥2॥
पुरा विनिहते वृत्रे दैत्या विगतनायकाः ॥
अब्दुर्गं सागरं कृत्वा रात्रौ निघ्नन्ति वै प्रजाः ॥ 3 ॥
सुरैः सर्वैः समागम्य तथाऽयं न परैर्वधम् ॥
समुद्रोदकपानाय अगस्त्यश्चोदितस्तदा ॥ 4 ॥
देवकर्मप्रमुदितस्तदागस्त्यमुनिर्नृप ॥
पीत्वा चकार राजेन्द्र निस्तोयं सलिलाशयम्॥। 5 ॥
देवैश्च निहता दैत्या निस्तोये सलिलाशये ॥
ततः कदाचिद्विन्ध्यस्तु जगादार्कनिशाकरौ ॥ 6 ॥
मेरुं त्यक्त्वा महाभागौ मम यात प्रदक्षिणम् ॥
ऊचतुस्तौ तदा विन्ध्यमावयोस्तु वशं गिरे ॥ 7 ॥
1.179.m:
1.213
Śailūṣa said:
How was Sumālī formerly struck down in battle by Viṣṇu? / Dispel this doubt of mine; he is heard of as one of mighty strength.
Nāḍāyana said:
This tale, O tiger among kings, was told long ago by the wise Agastya / to Rāma, O hero; listen to it as I relate it.
Formerly, when Vṛtra was slain, the Daityas, deprived of their leader, / made the ocean their water-fortress and slaughtered the creatures at night.
When all the gods assembled, since their destruction could not be achieved by other means, / Agastya was then urged to drink the ocean waters.
Delighted by the work of the gods, the sage Agastya then, O king, / drank it, O best of kings, and made the reservoir of water dry.
And the Daityas were slain by the gods in that waterless reservoir of water. / Then, once upon a time, the Vindhya mountain addressed the sun and the moon:
"O illustrious ones, leaving Meru aside, circumambulate me!" / Those two then said to the Vindhya: "O mountain, it is not in our power.

1.179.d:
तेन पन्थाः कृतोऽस्माकं येनेदं निर्मितं जगत् ॥
एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु विध्न्यस्तु तपस्तप्त्वा पितामहात् ॥ 8 ॥
इषुपातमथोच्छ्रायं प्रत्यहं समवाप्तवान् ॥
ततः कतिपयाहेन दिशमावृत्य दक्षिणाम् ॥ 9 ॥
आवृत्य तस्थौ पन्थानं दिवाकरनिशाभृतोः ॥
ततोऽन्धमभवत्सर्वो भूर्लोकः पार्थिवोत्तम ॥ 1.213.10 ॥
प्रेरितो देववाक्येन ततोऽगस्त्यो महातपाः ॥
गत्वोवाच तदा विन्ध्यं तीर्थयात्रां करोम्यहम् ॥ 11 ॥।
मत्कृते ह्रस्वतां गच्छ येन यास्याम्यहं सुखी ॥
ज्ञात्वा ततः प्रभावं तु सोऽगस्त्यस्य महागिरिः ॥ 12 ॥
जगाम ह्रस्वतां शीघ्रमगस्त्योऽपि तदा ययौ ॥
दक्षिणाशां परित्यज्य न यावदहमागतः ॥ 13 ॥
सपुत्रदारस्तावत्त्वं ह्रस्व एव भवाऽचल ॥
एवमुक्त्वा स विन्ध्यन्तु सदारापत्यबान्धवम् ॥ 14 ॥
1.179.m:
Our path was made by him by whom this world was created." / Having heard this, Vindhya, having performed austerities, from the Grandfather [Brahmā]
obtained an increase in height of an arrow's flight every day. / Then, after several days, obstructing the southern quarter,
he stood blocking the path of the sun and the moon. / Then the entire realm of earth became dark, O foremost of kings.
Urged by the word of the gods, Agastya of great ascetic power
then went and said to the Vindhya: “I am undertaking a pilgrimage to holy fords.
For my sake, become low, so that I may pass through with ease.”
Then, recognizing the spiritual power of Agastya, that great mountain
swiftly became low, and Agastya then departed.
“Until I return, leaving the southern quarter,
remain low, O mountain, along with your sons and wives!”
Having thus spoken to the Vindhya together with his wife, offspring, and kin,

जगाम दक्षिणामाशां तमुवाच पितामहः ॥
देवकार्यं महद्ब्रह्मंस्त्वया कृतमिदं शुभम् ॥ 15 ॥
तस्मात्स्थानं च ते दद्मि वैश्वानरपथाद्बहिः ॥
दिव्यदेहो भवांस्तत्र विमानवरमास्थितः ॥ 16 ॥
दक्षिणां भूषय दिशमस्तोदयसमन्वितः ॥
प्रसादमम्भसां शैत्यं निर्विषत्वं तवोदये ॥ 17 ॥
भविष्यत्यमलप्रज्ञ मत्प्रसादात्तवैव तु ॥
शरत्सु मुदितो वसन्तेस्तमयं व्रज ॥ 18 ॥
प्राकाम्ययुक्तश्च तथा समग्रां वसुधां चर ॥
प्रधानमूर्तिर्यावत्त्वं सदारापत्यबान्धवः ॥ 19 ॥
नाक्रमिष्यति वै विन्ध्यं तावद्विन्ध्याचलः स्थितः ॥
प्राकाम्यमूर्तियुक्ते तु यत्र क्वचन संस्थिते ॥ 1.213.20 ॥
त्वयि विन्ध्यो महाशैलो वृद्धिं न स गमिष्यति ॥
इल्वलश्चापि दुर्मेधा भ्रात्रा वै मेषरूपिणा ॥ ॥ 21 ॥
1.179.m:
he went to the southern quarter. Pitāmaha said to him:
“A great and auspicious task for the gods has been accomplished by you, O holy one.
Therefore, I grant you an abode outside the path of Vaiśvānara.
There, having assumed a divine body, mounted on an excellent aerial chariot,
adorn the southern quarter, possessed of rising and setting.
At your rising, there shall be clarity of waters, coolness, and freedom from poison,
O you of immaculate wisdom, through my grace alone.
Rejoicing in the autumns, set in the spring.
Endowed with unobstructed will, wander over the entire earth.
As long as you, along with your wife, children, and kin, in your primary form,
do not cross the Vindhya, the Vindhya mountain shall remain as it is.
Moreover, while you, possessing an embodiment of unobstructed will, abide anywhere at all,
that great mountain Vindhya will not attain growth.
And when the foolish Ilvala, by means of his brother in the form of a ram,

1.179.m:

Vātāpi, having burst open their bellies, came out again—
I am pleased with that which was done by you when he was thus slaying brahmins,
[namely] the refuge [granted to them], and with the checking of the Vindhya.
Since, having reached the autumn season, O brahmin, at your new rising,
you shall receive worship in the world by my grace, O foremost of the twice-born.
And those who will worship you with perfumes, garlands, fruits, and unbroken grains,
with curd, gold, gems, and abundant sweet milk-rice,
with full jars accompanied by gourds, with umbrellas, sandals, and staffs,
with a cow, with a bull, with delicacies, with garments, and with gold,
and by renouncing a single fruit for a year,
by honoring the foremost brahmins and by proclaiming your deeds,
they will always obtain sons, wealth, and health,
the highest lifespan in the world, and invincibility against enemies,

येन क्रतुशतैरिष्टं तपस्तप्तं तथा महत् ॥ 1.213.30 ॥
तेन स्वतपसा सृष्टा लोपामुद्रा प्रियंवदा ॥
विदर्भराजतनया धर्मपत्नी तथात्मनः ॥ 31 ॥
दृढस्युस्तनयस्तस्य तपस्वी च महातपाः ॥
प्रमुचुर्मुमुचुश्चैव तन्मुचुश्च महातपाः ॥ 32 ॥

अभेद्यं कवचं दत्तं तथाऽक्षय्ये महेषुधी ॥ 33 ॥
रामलक्ष्मणयोस्तेन धनुषी च महाबले ॥
घोरेणाप्यथ संयुक्तः स च वैष्णवतेजसा ॥ 34 ॥
कर्मणा कीर्तनं यस्य नरो वर्षशतैरपि ॥
कर्तुं शक्तो न सहते प्राकाम्ये चैव रावणे ॥ 35 ॥
1.179.m:
good fortune, extensive desires, and likewise the increase of dharma.”
Having spoken thus, the Blessed One vanished right there.
Agastya too, of great ascetic power, reached that abode,
he by whom sacrifices were offered with hundreds of rites, and by whom great austerity was performed.
By his own ascetic power was created the sweet-speaking Lopāmudrā,
the daughter of the king of Vidarbha, as his lawful wife.
His son was Dṛḍhasyu, an ascetic of great austerity;
Pramucu, Mumucu, and Tanmucu of great austerity,
and the learned Svastyātreya was the disciple of that great-souled one.
Impenetrable armor was given [by him], as well as two inexhaustible great quivers,
and two exceedingly strong bows to Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa;
and he was endowed with fierce Vaiṣṇava splendour.
Even in hundreds of years, a man is not able to recount
the deeds of him who could not tolerate Rāvaṇa’s uncontrolled power.

1.179.m:
Then, at the conclusion of a tale, the scion of Raghu questioned him
about the slaying of Mālī by Viṣṇu; hear what was spoken by him to him.
Understand that very thing: the exceedingly terrifying slaying of the lord of the hordes of rākṣasas,
which the great-souled sage, whose splendor was equal to the moon, sun, and fire, told to the delight of the Raghus.
Agastya said:
O king of kings, Mālī, Sumālī, and Mālyavān, fierce in battle,
having reached the fortress of Laṅkā, dwelt [there], conversing wonderfully with one another.
Mālī and Sumālī were of wicked conduct, tormenting the deities,
even though always restrained by that Mālyavān, O king.
Terrified of the two, Brahmā was informed by the gods along with their purpose.
Having gone together with Brahmā, the destroyer of Tripura was informed.
Accompanied by Brahmā and Īśa, the gods, having taken refuge in Viṣṇu,
went to make their petition to Acyuta residing in the salt-water ocean.
And they saw, O best of the Raghus, the ocean of water that was drunk,
as if leaping with the wind through dancing swarms of waves,

विष्णोर्वराहवपुषा विक्षोभितजलाविलम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.179.m:
as if laughing with masses of foam, stumbling in caverns,
as if shoreless, roaring, filled with multitudes of diverse aquatic creatures,
as if calling out to the immortals with its swaying wave-hands;
and foaming, scattered, gathered together, and raised high
were seen its waves, like moving mountains.
Timiṅgilas and turtles, and also timis and timiṅgilas,
and sea-monsters were seen submerged in the water like mountains;
and thousands of conches submerged in the waters on all sides
were seen like stars obscured by thin clouds at night.
Here sleeping, there roaring, here swirling, there tumbling,
the lords of the gods saw that ocean resembling a drunken man,
here settled by Daityas, and there by the enemy of the Daityas,
and here with terrifying serpents, endowed with immense depth,
its waters turbid and agitated by the boar-form of Viṣṇu,

1.179.d:
अनासादितबाधं च वर्षाणां शतपत्रिणा ॥
तेन देवातिदेवेन विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना ॥13॥
नित्यमन्तरसंस्थेन निर्मलीकृतविग्रहम् ॥
शक्रवज्रभयत्रस्यमानशैलशता कुलम् ॥ 14 ॥
विद्रुमाम्बरमाप्लुष्टसदृशाकारविद्रुमम् ॥
पूर्णचन्द्रकलङ्कस्य क्षालनेप्सुरिवोद्धतैः ॥ 15 ॥
खमाक्रमति कल्लोलैः पौर्णमासीषु यः सदा ॥
असंख्यातं तरङ्गौघैः संक्रान्तशशिमण्डलम् ॥ 16॥
हसन्तं वान्तरिक्षस्य श्रियमेवेन्दुधारिणः ॥
दिग्भागदानकालेषु युक्तश्चन्दनवा रिणा ॥
सुप्यते च यथा यत्र सततं दानवारिणा ॥ 17 ॥
तमन्तरिक्षप्रतिमं विशाललोलोर्मिमालाकुलदिग्विभागम् ॥
समुद्रमासाद्य दिवौकसस्त मातस्थुरुग्रं तपसोग्रसत्त्वाः ॥ 18॥

1.179.m:
and suffering no impediment from a hundred-feathered arrow of rains
by that god of gods, Viṣṇu, the mighty lord.
whose body is made pure by him who constantly dwells within,
which is crowded with hundreds of mountains terrified by fear of Śakra's thunderbolt,
whose clothes are corals and whose corals resemble burnt appearances,
as if wishing to wash away the stain of the full moon with raised [surges],
which constantly assaults the sky on full-moon days with high waves,
wherein the disc of the moon is mirrored countless times by floods of billows,
mocking, as it were, the beauty of the moon-bearing firmament,
mingled with sandalwood-water at the times of giving gifts in various directions,
and where the enemy of the Danavas constantly sleeps;
Reaching that ocean resembling the firmament, whose quarters were bewildered by a vast garland of restless waves,
those fierce-spirited dwellers of heaven entered upon severe ascetic penance.
Agastya said:
Pleased by the gods through their ascetic penance, Janārdana, the god of gods,
left his abode in the great waters and showed himself to the deities.

1.179.d:
ते च तं विबुधारिघ्नं धरणीपातपांसुलैः ॥
जानुपाणिललाटान्तैः प्रणेमुर्मुदिता हरिम्॥2॥
तुष्टुवुश्च तथा वाग्भिरथोचुः स्वप्रयोजनम् ॥
वधार्थं देवदेवस्य सुकेशतनयान्प्रति ॥ 3 ॥
प्रतिजज्ञे तदा तेषां देवो मालिवधं हरिः ॥
यूयं सुमालिनिधने शक्ताः स्थ सुरसत्तमाः ॥ 4 ॥
माल्यवानप्यवध्योऽसौ सततं धर्मवत्सलः ॥
एवमुक्त्वा ततस्तार्क्ष्यमाह्वयामास केशवः॥5॥
तमारुरोह सर्वात्मा काञ्चनं विनतासुतम् ॥
शंखचक्रगदापद्मलाच्छितो मधुसूदनः॥ ॥6॥
अतसीकुसुमश्यामः काञ्चने खगमे स्थितः ॥
श्रियमूहे सतोयस्य तोयदस्य सविद्युतः ॥7॥
किरीटकौस्तुभधरं वरभूषणभूषितम् ॥
विहङ्ग वरमारूढमनुजग्मुर्दिवौकसः ॥ 8 ॥
सुधावदातसत्पक्षैर्वितताम्बरधाविभिः ॥
हंसैस्तमन्वयाद्ब्रह्मा जटामण्डलदुर्दृशः ॥ 9 ॥
1.179.m:
And with joy, their knees, hands, and foreheads dusty from falling to the earth,
they bowed to Hari, the slayer of the enemies of the gods,
and praised [him] with hymns, and then declared their purpose:
for the slaying of the sons of Sukeśa, to the god of gods.
Then the divine Hari promised them the slaying of Māli:
“O foremost of gods, you are capable of the destruction of Sumāli.
Mālyavān too is not to be slain, for he is ever devoted to dharma.”
Having spoken thus, Keśava then summoned Tārkṣya.
The Universal Self mounted the golden son of Vinatā;
Madhusūdana, marked with conch, discus, mace, and lotus,
dark as an atasī blossom, seated upon the golden bird,
borne the splendor of a raincloud laden with water, accompanied by lightning.
Wearing a diadem and the Kaustubha, adorned with exquisite ornaments,
mounted upon the foremost of birds, the dwellers of heaven followed him.
Difficult to behold because of his mass of matted locks, Brahmā followed him
on swans with noble wings white as nectar, flying across the wide sky.

1.179.d:
चन्द्ररश्मिप्रतीकाशनिबिडाङ्गककुद्मिकः ॥
हरस्तृतीयनेत्रार्चिर्विदारितनभो ययौ ॥ 1.215.10 ॥
महेन्द्रनेत्रसंकाशकलापाटोपरोधिना ॥
स्कन्दस्तमन्वयौ तस्मा न्मयूरेण षडाननः ॥ 11 ॥
विनायकान्कर्तुमना राक्षसेन्द्रान्विनायकः ॥
वायुमण्डलमारूढः प्रययावनुमाधवम् ॥ 12 ॥
वह्रिज्वालावली पुञ्जसमकेसरमालिना ॥
सिंहेनानुययौ देवी भद्रकाली जनार्दनम् ॥ 13 ॥
वरस्त्रीकुचसंकाशकुम्भैरावणपृष्टगः ॥
किरीटी वज्रपाणिस्तमन्वयौ त्रिदशाधिपः ॥ 14 ॥
वह्निस्तमन्वयौ देवं शुकयानेन पार्थिव ॥
सेन्द्रगोपगणाकीर्णशाद्वलस्थलशोभिना ॥ 15 ॥
गिरिकूटसमाकारं शृङ्ग भूषितमस्तकम् ॥
वैवस्वतोऽपि महिषमारुह्यानुययौ हरिम् ॥ 16 ॥
शङ्कुकर्णो महाग्रीवो वरेभस्कन्धसंस्थितः ॥
पश्चादनुययौ देवं विरूपाक्षो महाबलः ॥ 17 ॥
1.179.m:
Hara went, rending the sky with the blazing light of his third eye,
possessing a hump of compact limbs resembling the rays of the moon.
With a peacock that obstructed [sight] with the display of its plumage resembling the eyes of Mahendra,
the six-faced Skanda then followed him.
Intending to render the lords of the rākṣasas leaderless, Vināyaka,
mounted upon the realm of wind, set out behind Mādhava.
On a lion whose mane was like a mass of blazing clusters of fire,
the goddess Bhadrakālī followed Janārdana.
Seated on the back of Airāvaṇa, whose frontal globes resembled the breasts of a lovely woman,
the diadem-wearing lord of the thirty [gods] followed him with thunderbolt in hand.
Fire followed the god upon a vehicle of parrots, O king,
shining like a grassy plot strewn with swarms of indragopa beetles.
Vaivasvata also, mounting a buffalo that resembled a mountain peak
and had its head adorned with horns, followed Hari.
With peg-like ears and a huge neck, seated upon the shoulder of an excellent elephant,
the mighty Virūpākṣa followed behind the god.

1.179.d:
महायानेन रम्येण मनोमारुतरंहसा ॥
वरुणोऽनुययौ पश्चात्स्निग्धवैदूर्यसन्निभः ॥ 18 ॥
मनःशीघ्रगतिर्देवो वायु मण्डलमध्यगः ॥
वायुश्चानुययौ पश्चाद्वायुपूर्णशुभांशुकः ॥ 19 ॥
धनदो नरयानेन सर्वरत्नोज्वलात्मना ॥
गोविन्दमनुवव्राज श्रिया परमया युतः ॥ 1.215.20 ॥
सप्ताश्वमेकचक्रं च रथमारुह्य भानुमान् ॥
तथैवानुययौ देवं प्रभामण्डलदुर्दृशः ॥ 21 ॥
चन्द्रश्चण्डप्रभावारो दशभिस्तुरगो त्तमैः ॥
मनोजवेन च तथा रथेनानुययौ हरिम् ॥ 22 ॥
तुरङ्गवरमारुह्य भास्करप्रतिमाकृतिः ॥
तमन्वयौ तदा राजन्प्रचण्डो रविनन्दनः ॥ ॥ 23 ॥
चतुर्भिः कुञ्जरैर्युक्तं रथमास्थाय सत्वरा ॥
तमन्वयौ धरादेवी देवं त्रिदशपूजितम् ॥ 24 ॥
सङ्कल्परथमारुह्य व्यवसाय पुरःसरः ॥
मनोरथेनानुययौ कामदेवोऽपि केशवम्॥ 25 ॥
1.179.m:
Varuṇa, resembling smooth cat's-eye gem, followed behind
in a splendid, magnificent carriage swift as the mind and the wind.
The god Vāyu, moving as swiftly as thought, standing in the midst of his sphere of wind,
followed behind with his auspicious garments filled with wind.
Dhanada, upon a human-borne chariot brilliant with every jewel,
accompanied Govinda, endowed with supreme splendor.
Mounted upon a single-wheeled chariot with seven horses, the Sun,
difficult to behold with his orb of radiance, likewise followed the god.
And the Moon, with terrifying force and brilliance, followed Hari
with ten foremost horses and with a chariot swift as thought.
Mounted upon an excellent steed, his form resembling the sun,
the fierce son of the Sun then followed him, O king.
Quickly mounting a chariot yoked with four elephants,
the goddess Earth followed the god worshipped by the thirty [gods].
Mounted on a chariot of resolve, preceded by determination,
even Kāmadeva followed Keśava upon the chariot of his desire,

पुष्पेषोरपि यस्याज्ञां बिभर्ति सकलं जगत् ॥
अनालस्यं समारूढा तथा देवी सरस्वती ॥ ॥ 26 ॥
अन्यया पुण्डरीकाक्षं शरणागतवत्सलम ॥

वाजियुक्तै रथैः शीघ्ररमन्वयुः पुरुषो त्तमम्॥
देवाश्चैकोनपञ्चाशन्मरुतश्चारुमण्डलाः॥28॥
अनुजग्मुः सुराः कृष्णं वायुमण्डलमध्यगाः ॥
अनुजग्मुस्तमादित्या रथैः काञ्चन सुप्रभैः ॥ 29 ॥
वसवोऽङ्गिरसः साध्या विश्वेदेवास्तथाश्विनौ ॥
भृगवश्चाश्वसंयुक्तै रथैस्तं देवमन्वयुः ॥ 1.215.30 ॥
रुद्राश्चानुययुर्देवं बलोदग्रैः ककुद्मिभिः ॥
तथैवान्ये बलोदग्रा देवा देवानुयायिनः ॥ 31 ॥
गर्दभैः शिशुमारैश्च महोष्ट्रैर्महिषोरगैः ॥
सिंहव्याघ्रतरक्ष्वृक्षगजवानर मर्कटैः ॥ 32 ॥
1.179.m:
even he of flower-arrows whose command the entire universe obeys;
and mounting diligence, the goddess Sarasvatī [followed].
She followed the lotus-eyed one who is affectionate to those who seek refuge.
Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Rāhu, Ketu, and Saturn,
with chariots yoked with horses, swiftly followed Puruṣottama.
And the gods, the forty-nine Maruts of beautiful circles,
the gods situated in the sphere of the wind, followed Kṛṣṇa.
The Ādityas followed him in chariots of bright gold.
The Vasus, the Aṅgirases, the Sādhyas, the Viśvedevas, and the two Aśvins,
and the Bhṛgus followed that god in chariots joined with horses.
And the Rudras followed the god upon bulls prominent in strength;
likewise other gods fierce in strength, who followed the god,
upon donkeys, porpoises, large camels, buffaloes, serpents,
lions, tigers, hyenas, bears, elephants, monkeys, and baboons,

gītavādyaiḥ sumadhuraiḥ sevamānā janārdanam ..
prahṛṣṭāḥ prayayustatra gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ .. 35 ..
tapaḥ satyaṃ kṣamā dānaṃ vratāni vividhāni ca ..
yajñāṅgāni ca sarvāṇi kālasyāvayavāstathā .. 36 ..
saṃvatsarāstathā māsāḥ pakṣau ca karaṇaiḥ saha ..
yugāyanamuhūrtāśca śāstrāṇi vividhāni ca .. 37 ..
mūrtimanti tathāstrāṇi śastrāṇi ca jagatpateḥ ..
samudrapathataddvīpaśākhināṃ vigrahāṇi ca .. 38 ..
1.179.d:
चमरैः सृमरैश्चैव गोधामार्जारशल्लकैः ॥
विविधैः पक्षियानैश्च तेऽनुजग्मुर्जनार्दनम् ॥ 33 ॥
सिद्धमार्गेण सिद्धाश्च प्रययुर्मुनयस्तथा ॥
स्तुवन्तः पुण्डरीकाक्षं देवसंघभयापहम् ॥ 34 ॥
गीतवाद्यैः सुमधुरैः सेवमाना जनार्दनम् ॥
प्रहृष्टाः प्रययुस्तत्र गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणाः ॥ 35 ॥
तपः सत्यं क्षमा दानं व्रतानि विविधानि च ॥
यज्ञाङ्गानि च सर्वाणि कालस्यावयवास्तथा ॥ 36 ॥
संवत्सरास्तथा मासाः पक्षौ च करणैः सह ॥
युगायनमुहूर्ताश्च शास्त्राणि विविधानि च ॥ 37 ॥
मूर्तिमन्ति तथास्त्राणि शस्त्राणि च जगत्पतेः ॥
समुद्रपथतद्द्वीपशाखिनां विग्रहाणि च ॥ 38 ॥
1.179.m:
upon yaks, antelopes, monitor lizards, cats, and porcupines,
and upon various bird-mounts, they followed Janārdana.
Along the path of the perfected ones, the Siddhas and sages also proceeded,
praising the lotus-eyed one who removes the fear of the hosts of gods.
Serving Janārdana with exceedingly sweet songs and instrumental music,
troops of gandharvas and apsarases went thither rejoicing.
Austerity, truth, forbearance, charity, and various vows,
all limbs of the sacrifice, and the divisions of time,
years, months, the two fortnights along with the karaṇas,
ages, solstices, muhūrtas, and various sacred scriptures,
and the embodied divine missiles and weapons of the Lord of the Universe,
and the personified forms of the ocean paths, its islands, and its trees [followed].

1.179.s:
varṣāṇāṃ ca śarīrāṇi pitṝṇāṃ ca tathā gaṇāḥ ..
nakṣatrāṇi diśaścaiva vidiśaśca mahīpate .. 39 ..
1.179.d:
वर्षाणां च शरीराणि पितॄणां च तथा गणाः ॥
नक्षत्राणि दिशश्चैव विदिशश्च महीपते ॥ 39 ॥
1.179.m: And the bodies of the years, and likewise the hosts of the ancestors, / the lunar mansions, the cardinal directions, and the intermediate directions, O king;

1.179.s:
devā vanaspatiścaiva yāśca lokasya mātaraḥ ..
devadaityagaṇā ye ca tathā pitṛgaṇāśca ye .. 1.215.40 ..
1.179.d:
देवा वनस्पतिश्चैव याश्च लोकस्य मातरः ॥
देवदैत्यगणा ये च तथा पितृगणाश्च ये ॥ 1.215.40 ॥
1.179.m: the gods, the lord of the forest, and those who are the mothers of the world, / the hosts of gods and daityas, and likewise those hosts of ancestors;

1.179.s:
gandharvayakṣanāgānāṃ gaṇā ye ca nareśvara ..
ghorā vyādhigaṇāścaiva kālapāśaiḥ sudāruṇaiḥ .. 41 ..
1.179.d:
गन्धर्वयक्षनागानां गणा ये च नरेश्वर ॥
घोरा व्याधिगणाश्चैव कालपाशैः सुदारुणैः ॥ 41 ॥
1.179.m: and the hosts of gandharvas, yakṣas, and nāgas, O lord of men; / and the terrible hosts of diseases with their most dread nooses of time;

1.179.s:
mṛtyurdaṇḍastathā krodho jarā ca manujeśvara ..
anvayuḥ puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ rakṣogaṇavadhaiṣiṇam .. 42 ...
1.179.d:
मृत्युर्दण्डस्तथा क्रोधो जरा च मनुजेश्वर ॥
अन्वयुः पुण्डरीकाक्षं रक्षोगणवधैषिणम् ॥ 42 ॥।
1.179.m: Death, Punishment, Wrath, and Old Age, O lord of men, / followed the lotus-eyed one who desired the slaughter of the host of rākṣasas.

1.179.s:
jayaśrīragratastasya prayāti raghunandana ..
saritaśca tathā yānaiḥ sarvalokasya mātaraḥ ..43..
1.179.d:
जयश्रीरग्रतस्तस्य प्रयाति रघुनन्दन ॥
सरितश्च तथा यानैः सर्वलोकस्य मातरः ॥43॥
1.179.m: The Fortune of Victory marched before him, O descendant of Raghu, / and likewise the rivers, the mothers of all the world, upon their vehicles.

1.179.s:
makareṇa yayau gaṅgā kālindī kacchapena tu..
sārasenāpi sarayūḥ śiśumāreṇa gomatī .. 44 ..
1.179.d:
मकरेण ययौ गङ्गा कालिन्दी कच्छपेन तु॥
सारसेनापि सरयूः शिशुमारेण गोमती ॥ 44 ॥
1.179.m: Gaṅgā rode upon a makara, but Kālindī on a tortoise; / Sarayū upon a crane, and Gomatī on a dolphin;

1.179.s:
godāvarī ca khaḍgena mayūreṇa sarasvatī ..
kakudminā śatadruśca vipāśā turageṇa ca .. 45 ..
1.179.d:
गोदावरी च खड्गेन मयूरेण सरस्वती ॥
ककुद्मिना शतद्रुश्च विपाशा तुरगेण च ॥ 45 ॥
1.179.m: Godāvarī upon a rhinoceros, Sarasvatī on a peacock; / Śatadru upon a humped bull, and Vipāśā on a horse;

1.179.s:
candrabhāgā ca siṃhena dantinerāvatī tathā ..
sindhurvyāghreṇa matsyena vitastā ca tathā yayau .. 46 ..
1.179.d:
चन्द्रभागा च सिंहेन दन्तिनेरावती तथा ॥
सिन्धुर्व्याघ्रेण मत्स्येन वितस्ता च तथा ययौ ॥ 46 ॥
1.179.m: Candrabhāgā upon a lion, and Irāvatī likewise on an elephant; / Sindhu went upon a tiger, and Vitastā likewise on a fish;

1.179.s:
devikā caiva haṃsena puruṣeṇa ca gaṇḍakī ..
mahiṣeṇa payoṣṇī ca kāverī vṛṣabheṇa tu .. 47 ..
1.179.d:
देविका चैव हंसेन पुरुषेण च गण्डकी ॥
महिषेण पयोष्णी च कावेरी वृषभेण तु ॥ 47 ॥
1.179.m: Devikā upon a goose, and Gaṇḍakī on a man; / Payoṣṇī upon a buffalo, but Kāverī on a bull;

1.179.s:
hiraṇvatī suparṇena cakreṇekṣumatī nadī ..
bhujagena ca pārṇāśā varāheṇa ca kauśikī.. 48 ..
1.179.d:
हिरण्वती सुपर्णेन चक्रेणेक्षुमती नदी ॥
भुजगेन च पार्णाशा वराहेण च कौशिकी॥ 48 ॥
1.179.m: Hiraṇvatī upon a bird of fair plumage, the river Ikṣumatī on a wheel; / Pārṇāśā upon a serpent, and Kauśikī on a boar;

1.179.s:
vedasmṛtirmayūreṇa sāraṅgeṇa ca narmadā ..
jīvajīvakamārūḍhā sītāpi prayayau nadī .. 49 ..
1.179.d:
वेदस्मृतिर्मयूरेण सारङ्गेण च नर्मदा ॥
जीवजीवकमारूढा सीतापि प्रययौ नदी ॥ 49 ॥
1.179.m: Vedasmṛti upon a peacock, and Narmadā on a spotted deer; / mounted on a jīvañjīvaka bird, the river Sītā also went forth;

1.179.s:
hrādinī ca sarorūḍhā sṛmareṇa ca pāvanī ..
śaśakenāpi lauhityā nadī sindhurgajena ca .. 1.215.50 ..
1.179.d:
ह्रादिनी च सरोरूढा सृमरेण च पावनी ॥
शशकेनापि लौहित्या नदी सिन्धुर्गजेन च ॥ 1.215.50 ॥
1.179.m: Hrādinī mounted on a lake-lotus, and Pāvanī on a sṛmara deer; / the river Lauhityā upon a hare, and Sindhu on an elephant;

1.179.s:
urabhreṇa tathā cakṣuḥ sītā cājena rāghava ..
gautamī kukkuṭenāpi cāṣeṇa ca dṛṣadvatī .. 51 ..
1.179.d:
उरभ्रेण तथा चक्षुः सीता चाजेन राघव ॥
गौतमी कुक्कुटेनापि चाषेण च दृषद्वती ॥ 51 ॥
1.179.m: Cakṣu upon a ram, and Sītā on a goat, O descendant of Raghu; / Gautamī upon a rooster, and Dṛṣadvatī on a blue jay.

1.179.s:
svaiḥ svairyānaistathaivānyāḥ prayayurnimnagā harima ..
devānuyātrāghoṣeṇa vāditrāṇāṃ raveṇa ca ..52..
1.179.d:
स्वैः स्वैर्यानैस्तथैवान्याः प्रययुर्निम्नगा हरिम ॥
देवानुयात्राघोषेण वादित्राणां रवेण च ॥52॥
1.179.m: In the same way other streams set forth with Hari upon their respective vehicles, / amidst the roar of the gods' procession and the sound of musical instruments.

1.179.s:
stūyamāno dvijāgryaiśca prayayau kamalekṣaṇaḥ ..
tadbalo yamaparyantaṃ devagandharvasaṃkulam .. 53 ..
1.179.d:
स्तूयमानो द्विजाग्र्यैश्च प्रययौ कमलेक्षणः ॥
तद्बलो यमपर्यन्तं देवगन्धर्वसंकुलम् ॥ 53 ॥
1.179.m: Praised by the foremost twice-born, the lotus-eyed one advanced; / his army, dense with gods and gandharvas, extended as far as the realm of Yama.

1.179.s:
ātapatraiḥ patākābhiḥ svacihnaiśca virājitam ..
kiṅkiṇīśatasaṃghoṣaṃ prayayāvanukeśavam .. 54 ...
1.179.d:
आतपत्रैः पताकाभिः स्वचिह्नैश्च विराजितम् ॥
किङ्किणीशतसंघोषं प्रययावनुकेशवम् ॥ 54 ॥।
1.179.m: Resplendent with parasols, banners, and their respective emblems, / echoing with the sound of hundreds of tiny bells, it marched behind Keśava.

1.179.s:
raśmyutkarairdevavibhūṣaṇānāṃ pradīpyamānaṃ kalanakādicitram..
balaṃ yayau tattridaśottamānāṃ nārāyaṇenā'pratimena guptam..55..
1.179.d:
रश्म्युत्करैर्देवविभूषणानां प्रदीप्यमानं कलनकादिचित्रम्॥
बलं ययौ तत्त्रिदशोत्तमानां नारायणेनाऽप्रतिमेन गुप्तम्॥55॥
1.179.m: Blazing with masses of rays from divine ornaments, variegated with various tinkling sounds, / that army of the foremost deities marched forth, protected by the peerless Nārāyaṇa.

1.180.s:
1.216
agastya uvāca ..
devatānāṃ samudyogaṃ śrutvā mālisumālinau ..
cakratuḥ pṛtanāṃ ghorāṃ tridaśairyuddhakāṅkṣiṇau .. 1 ..
1.180.d:
1.216
अगस्त्य उवाच ॥
देवतानां समुद्योगं श्रुत्वा मालिसुमालिनौ ॥
चक्रतुः पृतनां घोरां त्रिदशैर्युद्धकाङ्क्षिणौ ॥ 1 ॥
1.180.m: Agastya said: / Hearing of the enterprise of the gods, Māli and Sumāli, / eager for battle with the thirty [gods], marshalled a dreadful army.

1.180.s:
tau kruddhau bhrātarau śrīmānmālyavānvākyamabravīt ..
āśrayastridaśendrāṇāṃ sarvātmā madhusūdanaḥ .. 2 ..
1.180.d:
तौ क्रुद्धौ भ्रातरौ श्रीमान्माल्यवान्वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥
आश्रयस्त्रिदशेन्द्राणां सर्वात्मा मधुसूदनः ॥ 2 ॥
1.180.m: To those two enraged brothers the glorious Mālyavān spoke these words: / 'Madhusūdana is the refuge of the lords of the gods, the Self of all.

1.180.s:
tena yuddhaṃ na kartavyaṃ sa tu pūjyo jagatpatiḥ ..
agre tu praṇipātena taṃ yajāmo jagatpatim .. 3 ..
1.180.d:
तेन युद्धं न कर्तव्यं स तु पूज्यो जगत्पतिः ॥
अग्रे तु प्रणिपातेन तं यजामो जगत्पतिम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.180.m: No battle should be fought with him; he, the Lord of the World, is to be worshipped. / First, let us worship that Lord of the World by falling prostrate [before him].

1.180.s:
praṇipātaprasanno hi kāmāndāsyati keśavaḥ ..
viṣṇurhi maline citte'tvasmākaṃ nṛpa durjayaḥ .. 4..
1.180.d:
प्रणिपातप्रसन्नो हि कामान्दास्यति केशवः ॥
विष्णुर्हि मलिने चित्तेऽत्वस्माकं नृप दुर्जयः ॥ 4॥
1.180.m: For Keśava, pleased by prostration, will grant our desires; / but if our minds are impure, Viṣṇu is unconquerable by us, O king.

1.180.s:
jīvema suciraṃ kālaṃ sthitā devasya śāsane ..
prasīda rājanmā yuddhaṃ vraja devena viṣṇunā..5..
1.180.d:
जीवेम सुचिरं कालं स्थिता देवस्य शासने ॥
प्रसीद राजन्मा युद्धं व्रज देवेन विष्णुना॥5॥
1.180.m: We might live for a very long time abiding by the command of the god. / Be appeased, O king; do not go to war with the god Viṣṇu!

1.180.s:
yakṣāṇāṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca kuru śreyastathātmanaḥ ..
etaduktaṃ hitaṃ bhrātrā ruruce na ca tasya tat .. 6 ..
1.180.d:
यक्षाणां राक्षसानां च कुरु श्रेयस्तथात्मनः ॥
एतदुक्तं हितं भ्रात्रा रुरुचे न च तस्य तत् ॥ 6 ॥
1.180.m: Secure the welfare of the yakṣas and rākṣasas, as well as of yourself.' / This beneficial counsel, spoken by his brother, did not please him.

1.180.s:
mahatā ca sa sainyena prayayau yena keśavaḥ ..
tamanvayau mahātejā sumālī rākṣasādhipaḥ..7..
1.180.d:
महता च स सैन्येन प्रययौ येन केशवः ॥
तमन्वयौ महातेजा सुमाली राक्षसाधिपः॥7॥
1.180.m: And with a great army he marched to where Keśava was; / the mighty-spirited Sumāli, lord of the rākṣasas, followed him.

1.180.s:
pitṛtulyaśca sādhūnāṃ jyeṣṭhabhrātā gururmataḥ..
ādau vācyaṃ hitaṃ tasya kāryaṃ tadanuceṣṭitam..8..
1.180.d:
पितृतुल्यश्च साधूनां ज्येष्ठभ्राता गुरुर्मतः॥
आदौ वाच्यं हितं तस्य कार्यं तदनुचेष्टितम्॥8॥
1.180.m: For the virtuous, an elder brother is considered equal to a father, an elder; / first, beneficial advice should be spoken to him, and then one must act in accordance with him.

1.180.s:
etāṃ buddhiṃ samāsthāya niryāto mālyavānapi..
te rākṣasā saha bhrātrā bhīmanetrāgnibhūṣaṇāḥ ..9 ..
1.180.d:
एतां बुद्धिं समास्थाय निर्यातो माल्यवानपि॥
ते राक्षसा सह भ्रात्रा भीमनेत्राग्निभूषणाः ॥9 ॥
1.180.m: Adopting this resolution, Mālyavān also marched forth. / Together with his brother, those rākṣasas whose ornaments were fierce fiery eyes,

1.180.s:
koṭīśatena mukhyānāṃ rākṣasānāṃ vinirgatāḥ ..
nānāvidhogravasanā nānāpraharaṇāyudhāḥ .. 1.216.10 ..
1.180.d:
कोटीशतेन मुख्यानां राक्षसानां विनिर्गताः ॥
नानाविधोग्रवसना नानाप्रहरणायुधाः ॥ 1.216.10 ॥
1.180.m: set out with a hundred crores of foremost rākṣasas, / wearing varied and terrible garments, armed with varied striking weapons.

1.180.s:
nānāvāditraghoṣeṇa prayātā rākṣasādhipāḥ ..
nānāprakārairvividhaiḥ prāṇibhirbalavattaraiḥ .. 11 ..
1.180.d:
नानावादित्रघोषेण प्रयाता राक्षसाधिपाः ॥
नानाप्रकारैर्विविधैः प्राणिभिर्बलवत्तरैः ॥ 11 ॥
1.180.m: Amid the sound of varied musical instruments, the rākṣasa chiefs marched forth; / with diverse, varied, and exceedingly powerful creatures

1.180.s:
vāhanaiḥ prayayurghorā rākṣasāstridaśādhipam ..
gacchatastu balaughasya tadā tasyottarāṃ diśama ..
babhūvā'bhimukhaṃ ghoraṃ vanaṃ tridaśapālitam .. 12 ..
1.180.d:
वाहनैः प्रययुर्घोरा राक्षसास्त्रिदशाधिपम् ॥
गच्छतस्तु बलौघस्य तदा तस्योत्तरां दिशम ॥
बभूवाऽभिमुखं घोरं वनं त्रिदशपालितम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.180.m: as their mounts, the terrible rākṣasas advanced against the lord of the thirty [gods]. / As that flood of an army was marching toward the northern direction, / a dreadful forest protected by the thirty [gods] came into view before them.

1.180.s:
himācalasyottaradigvibhāge khasthe bale te puruṣau pravīra ..
jayārthamabhyudyatacāpadaṇḍau pracakraturyuddhamadīnasattvau .. 13 ..
1.217
agastya uvāca ..
tataḥ prāvartata raṇaṃ khasthayorbalayostayoḥ ..
nānāpraharaṇodagrabhujayorjayamicchatoḥ .. 1 ..
tadā balābhrasaṃcchanne gagane khaḍgavidyuti ..
tasminneva kṣaṇe jāto bhānumānnṛpa vidyatiḥ ..2..
calatkhaḍgalatāvidyutsamudyotitavigrahāt ..
raktavṛṣṭiḥ papātorvyāṃ balameghānuvigrahāt..3..
tataḥ śoṇitavarṣeṇa sicyamāne mahītale ..
grāvavṛṣṭirmahatyāsīcchāditaṃ bhūtalaṃ yayā .. 4 ..
āsīdagamyā vasudhā śoṇitaughapariplutā ..
rajasvaleva yuvatistadā tatra narādhipa .. 5 ..
sphuramāṇā vidṛśyante bāhavaścandanokṣitāḥ ..
khaḍgaprahārapatitāḥ pañcaśīrṣā ivoragāḥ .. 6 ..
1.180.d:
हिमाचलस्योत्तरदिग्विभागे खस्थे बले ते पुरुषौ प्रवीर ॥
जयार्थमभ्युद्यतचापदण्डौ प्रचक्रतुर्युद्धमदीनसत्त्वौ ॥ 13 ॥
1.217
अगस्त्य उवाच ॥
ततः प्रावर्तत रणं खस्थयोर्बलयोस्तयोः ॥
नानाप्रहरणोदग्रभुजयोर्जयमिच्छतोः ॥ 1 ॥
तदा बलाभ्रसंच्छन्ने गगने खड्गविद्युति ॥
तस्मिन्नेव क्षणे जातो भानुमान्नृप विद्यतिः ॥2॥
चलत्खड्गलताविद्युत्समुद्योतितविग्रहात् ॥
रक्तवृष्टिः पपातोर्व्यां बलमेघानुविग्रहात्॥3॥
ततः शोणितवर्षेण सिच्यमाने महीतले ॥
ग्राववृष्टिर्महत्यासीच्छादितं भूतलं यया ॥ 4 ॥
आसीदगम्या वसुधा शोणितौघपरिप्लुता ॥
रजस्वलेव युवतिस्तदा तत्र नराधिप ॥ 5 ॥
स्फुरमाणा विदृश्यन्ते बाहवश्चन्दनोक्षिताः ॥
खड्गप्रहारपतिताः पञ्चशीर्षा इवोरगाः ॥ 6 ॥
1.180.m:
In the northern quarter of the Himālayas, when the two armies stood in the sky, those two men, foremost heroes, / with their bows raised for victory, of undaunted spirit, joined battle.
Agastya said: / Then the battle commenced between those two armies stationed in the sky, / whose arms were upraised with varied striking weapons, wishing for victory.
Then, when the sky was covered with army-clouds, lit by the lightning of swords, / at that very moment the sun became devoid of light, O king.
From that body illuminated by the lightning-flashes of moving sword-blades, / from that cloud-like army, a rain of blood fell upon the earth.
Then, as the surface of the earth was being drenched with the shower of blood, / there was a great shower of stones, by which the ground was covered.
Inundated by floods of blood, the earth became impassable, / resembling a menstruating young woman at that time, O lord of men.
Arms smeared with sandalwood paste were seen quivering, / fallen under sword-blows like five-headed serpents.

1.180.s:
mukhāni danta pūrāṇi tathā sarudhirāṇi ca ..
( virejurdāḍimānīva pākaprasphuritāni vā .. 7 ..

vicchinnavāhanāṅgaiśca khamāsītsaṃkulaṃ tathā .. 8 ..)

1.180.d:
मुखानि दन्त पूराणि तथा सरुधिराणि च ॥
( विरेजुर्दाडिमानीव पाकप्रस्फुरितानि वा ॥ 7 ॥
निपतद्भिस्तथा छत्रैश्चामरैर्व्यजनैस्तथा ॥
विच्छिन्नवाहनाङ्गैश्च खमासीत्संकुलं तथा ॥ 8 ॥)
किरीटैः कुण्डलैर्हारैः केयूरैरङ्गदैस्तथा ॥
पात्यमानैः खमभवद्रश्मिपुञ्जविराजितम् ॥ 9 ॥
क्षुरप्रविनिकृत्तानि रुधिराक्ते महीतले ॥
लुठन्ति नागहस्तानि भोगिभोगनिभानि च ॥ 1.217.10 ॥
अदृष्ट्वा पतितानीह शिरांसि वसुधातले ॥
हत्वा वंशान्खमाजग्मुरन्वेषन्त इवासवः ॥11॥
शरीरैर्भूतलं प्राप्ता दिवं प्राप्ता शरीरिभिः ॥
अन्तरिक्षे विनिहिता लोकत्रयजिगीषवः॥
छिन्नराक्षसमूर्धानो गलद्रुधिरबिन्दवः ॥
न्यपतन्नुत्तरादेव श्येनैरुपहृताशयात् ॥ 13 ॥
1.180.m:
Faces filled with teeth and covered in blood / shone like pomegranates bursting open upon ripening.
With falling parasols, chowries, and fans, / and with the severed limbs of mounts, the sky was utterly congested.
With diadems, earrings, necklaces, upper-arm bracelets, and armlets / being cast down, the sky was resplendent with masses of rays.
Severed by crescent-shaped arrows on the blood-soaked earth, / elephants' trunks, resembling the coils of serpents, rolled about.
Not seeing their heads fallen here upon the surface of the earth, / having struck down the lineages, their life-breaths departed into the sky as if in search of them.
With their bodies they reached the surface of the earth, and with their souls they reached heaven; / fixed in the sky, wishing to conquer the three worlds, / the severed heads of the rakshasas, from which drops of blood dripped, / fell down from above, their entrails having been carried off by falcons.

1.180.s:
śyenānāṃ bhramatāṃ tatra rākṣasāmiṣalipsayā ..
babhūva sadṛśaṃ rūpaṃ śīrṣāṇāṃ bhramatāṃ tathā .. .. 14 ..
1.180.d:
श्येनानां भ्रमतां तत्र राक्षसामिषलिप्सया ॥
बभूव सदृशं रूपं शीर्षाणां भ्रमतां तथा ॥ ॥ 14 ॥
1.180.m: Of the falcons wheeling there in their desire for rakshasa-flesh, / the appearance became identical to that of the heads wheeling likewise.

1.180.s:
nikṛttāṅganipātena patitā bahavastadā ..
suṣupurgāṃ samāliṅgya kravyādā rudhirāvilāḥ .. 15 ..
1.180.d:
निकृत्ताङ्गनिपातेन पतिता बहवस्तदा ॥
सुषुपुर्गां समालिङ्ग्य क्रव्यादा रुधिराविलाः ॥ 15 ॥
1.180.m: Having fallen by the downpour of severed limbs, / many flesh-eaters, defiled with blood, then slept embracing the earth.

1.180.s:
nipatanmattamātaṅaprasphuratkumbhanirgatā ..
muktāphalairjahāsorvī śūrāliṅgananirvṛtā .. 16 ..
1.180.d:
निपतन्मत्तमातङप्रस्फुरत्कुम्भनिर्गता ॥
मुक्ताफलैर्जहासोर्वी शूरालिङ्गननिर्वृता ॥ 16 ॥
1.180.m: Emerging from the throbbing temples of falling rutting elephants, / the earth laughed with pearls, gratified by the embrace of the heroes.

1.180.s:
hṛtakuñjaradaṃtāgravinagnāṅgāsturaṅgamāḥ ..
āseduḥ sucireṇorvī nabhasyeva gatāsavaḥ ..17 ..
1.180.d:
हृतकुञ्जरदंताग्रविनग्नाङ्गास्तुरङ्गमाः ॥
आसेदुः सुचिरेणोर्वी नभस्येव गतासवः ॥17 ॥
1.180.m: Horses whose bodies were impaled on the tips of the tusks of slain elephants / reached the earth only after a long time, their lives having departed while still in the sky.

1.180.s:
saṃprāptarudhirāṃ bhūmiṃ raktāsyāstu niśācarāḥ ..
yayuḥ śarīrairnihatāḥ samare rudhirapriyāḥ .. 18 ..
1.180.d:
संप्राप्तरुधिरां भूमिं रक्तास्यास्तु निशाचराः ॥
ययुः शरीरैर्निहताः समरे रुधिरप्रियाः ॥ 18 ॥
1.180.m: Having reached the earth soaked in blood, the night-wanderers with blood-smeared faces, / fond of blood, fell in battle with their bodies slain.

1.180.s:
vartamāne tathā bhīme yuddhe bhīrubhayaṃkare ..
lokapālaśaravrātanirbhinnā rajanīcarāḥ .. 19 ..
1.180.d:
वर्तमाने तथा भीमे युद्धे भीरुभयंकरे ॥
लोकपालशरव्रातनिर्भिन्ना रजनीचराः ॥ 19 ॥
1.180.m: While that dreadful battle, terrifying even to the cowardly, was thus underway, / the night-wanderers, pierced by the volley of arrows of the World-Guardians,

1.180.s:
dudruvurbhayasaṃvignāstadā rāma diśo daśa ..
vipradrutaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasānāṃ divaukasaiḥ .. 1.217.20 ..
1.180.d:
दुद्रुवुर्भयसंविग्नास्तदा राम दिशो दश ॥
विप्रद्रुतं बलं दृष्ट्वा राक्षसानां दिवौकसैः ॥ 1.217.20 ॥
1.180.m: fled in all ten directions, agitated by fear, O Rāma. / Seeing the army of the rakshasas routed by the gods,

1.180.s:
sumālirmālyavadgupto mālī devānathābravīt ..
kirañcharaughairvimalaistailadhautaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ .. 21 ..
1.180.d:
सुमालिर्माल्यवद्गुप्तो माली देवानथाब्रवीत् ॥
किरञ्छरौघैर्विमलैस्तैलधौतैः शिलाशितैः ॥ 21 ॥
1.180.m: Mālī, protected by Sumālī and Mālyavat, then addressed the gods, / scattering showers of flawless arrows, washed with oil and sharpened on stone.

1.180.s:
sānujena raṇe muktā śaravṛṣṭirdurāsadā ..
saṃchādayāmāsa diśaḥ pradiśaśca divaukasām .. 22 ..
1.180.d:
सानुजेन रणे मुक्ता शरवृष्टिर्दुरासदा ॥
संछादयामास दिशः प्रदिशश्च दिवौकसाम् ॥ 22 ॥
1.180.m: Released by him and his younger brothers in battle, an irresistible rain of arrows / covered all the directions and intermediate directions of the gods.

1.180.s:
yathāśaktiśaravrātānvārayanto'pi devatāḥ ..
rākṣasendraśarairbhinnāḥ keśavaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ .. 23 ..
1.180.d:
यथाशक्तिशरव्रातान्वारयन्तोऽपि देवताः ॥
राक्षसेन्द्रशरैर्भिन्नाः केशवं शरणं ययुः ॥ 23 ॥
1.180.m: Even while warding off the multitudes of arrows according to their ability, the gods, / pierced by the shafts of the rakshasa lord, sought refuge with Keśava.

1.180.s:
sa nivārya tadā sarvaṃ devasainyaṃ patatriṇā ..
pratyudyayau yuge yodhāndhanuṣā sapatatriṇā .. 24 ..
1.180.d:
स निवार्य तदा सर्वं देवसैन्यं पतत्रिणा ॥
प्रत्युद्ययौ युगे योधान्धनुषा सपतत्रिणा ॥ 24 ॥
1.180.m: Having then checked the entire army of the gods with [his bird]-mount, / he advanced against the warriors in the battle with his bow and winged arrows.

1.180.s:
etasminneva kāle tu rakṣasāṃ pīnavakṣasām ..
vinivṛttaṃ balaṃ sarvamamaraiḥ samarotsukam .. 25 ..
1.180.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु रक्षसां पीनवक्षसाम् ॥
विनिवृत्तं बलं सर्वममरैः समरोत्सुकम् ॥ 25 ॥
1.180.m: At that very time, the entire army of the broad-chested rakshasas, / eager for battle, was turned back by the immortals.

1.180.s:
tadbalaṃ sakalaṃ cakre śaraiḥ śārṅgapracoditaiḥ ..
chādayāmāsa samare gobhiḥ sūrya ivāniśam .. 26 ..
1.180.d:
तद्बलं सकलं चक्रे शरैः शार्ङ्गप्रचोदितैः ॥
छादयामास समरे गोभिः सूर्य इवानिशम् ॥ 26 ॥
1.180.m: With his discus and arrows loosed from the bow Śārṅga, he covered that entire army / in battle constantly, like the sun with its rays.

1.180.s:
nānāpraharaṇodagragarjamāno janārdanam ..
saṃchādayāṃ tadā cakruḥ sarvaiḥ praharaṇotkaraiḥ .. 27 ..
1.180.d:
नानाप्रहरणोदग्रगर्जमानो जनार्दनम् ॥
संछादयां तदा चक्रुः सर्वैः प्रहरणोत्करैः ॥ 27 ॥
1.180.m: Roaring fiercely with diverse weapons, / they then covered Janārdana with showers of all kinds of weapons.

1.180.s:
saṃchādyamānaistairghoraiḥ keśavo rajanīcaraiḥ ..
jahāra śīrṣāṇi tadā teṣāṃ sannataparvabhiḥ .. 28 ..
1.180.d:
संछाद्यमानैस्तैर्घोरैः केशवो रजनीचरैः ॥
जहार शीर्षाणि तदा तेषां सन्नतपर्वभिः ॥ 28 ॥
1.180.m: As he was being overwhelmed by those terrible night-wanderers, Keśava / then severed their heads with straight-jointed arrows.

1.180.s:
rathanīḍe dhanurnyasya mālī rākṣasapuṅgavaḥ ..
suparṇaṃ tāḍayāmāsa gadayā bhīmavegayā .. 29 ..
1.180.d:
रथनीडे धनुर्न्यस्य माली राक्षसपुङ्गवः ॥
सुपर्णं ताडयामास गदया भीमवेगया ॥ 29 ॥
1.180.m: Placing his bow on the chariot-seat, Mālī, the foremost of the rakshasas, / struck Suparṇa with a club of terrible velocity.

1.180.s:
gadāprahārābhihatastārkṣyaḥ parapurañjaya ..
parāṅmukhaṃ raṇāccakre vedanārto janārdanam .. 1.217.30 ..
1.180.d:
गदाप्रहाराभिहतस्तार्क्ष्यः परपुरञ्जय ॥
पराङ्मुखं रणाच्चक्रे वेदनार्तो जनार्दनम् ॥ 1.217.30 ॥
1.180.m: Struck by the blow of the club, Tārkṣya, O conqueror of enemy cities, / turned away from the battle, pained with agony, turning Janārdana away.

1.180.s:
parāṅmukhe tadā tārkṣye parivṛttānano hariḥ ..
śīrṣaṃ jahāra cakreṇa rākṣasendrasya mālinaḥ .. 31 ..
1.180.d:
पराङ्मुखे तदा तार्क्ष्ये परिवृत्ताननो हरिः ॥
शीर्षं जहार चक्रेण राक्षसेन्द्रस्य मालिनः ॥ 31 ॥
1.180.m: While Tārkṣya was thus turned away, Hari, turning his face around, / severed the head of the rakshasa lord Mālī with his discus.

सकुण्डलं चारुकिरीटजुष्टं निशाचरेशस्य शिरः पृथिव्याम् ॥
निपातितं वीक्ष्य मुदान्वितान्ता नार्यो बभूबुस्त्रिदशोत्तमानाम् ॥32॥
1.218
॥ अगस्त्य उवाच ॥
हते मालिनि दैवेन सान्त्वितः पक्षिराडसौ ॥
जहार पक्षवातेन निवृत्तो रक्षसां बलम् ॥1॥
ते तार्क्ष्यपक्षवातेन शुष्कपर्णचयो यथा ॥
द्रुता राक्षसशार्दूलास्तदा राम दिशो दश ॥ 2 ॥
अविन्दमानास्ते शर्म वासुदेवभयार्दिताः ॥
पातालतलमासेदुः सर्व एव पृथक्पृथक् ॥ 3 ॥
त्रिदशान्त्सान्त्वयित्वा च विष्णुस्त्रिदशपूजितः ॥
अन्तर्धानं ययौ तत्र सर्वेषामेव पश्यताम् ॥ 4 ॥
लङ्कापि शून्या राजेन्द्र दत्ता वैश्रवणाय सा ॥
स्वयं विश्रवसस्तस्यः रावणेन हृता बलात् ॥ 5 ॥
विभीषणाय सा दत्ता त्वया हत्वा च रावणम् ॥
राम विष्णुः समुत्पन्नस्त्वं वधायेह रक्षसाम् ॥ 6 ॥
1.180.m:
Beholding the head of the lord of night-wanderers, adorned with earrings and a beautiful crest, / struck down upon the earth, the wives of the foremost gods became filled with joy.
Agastya said: / When Mālī was slain, that king of birds, consoled by the Lord, / turned back and swept away the army of the rakshasas with the wind of his wings.
Like a heap of dry leaves driven by the wind of Tārkṣya's wings, / those tigers among rakshasas then fled in all ten directions, O Rāma.
Finding no peace, afflicted by fear of Vāsudeva, / they all went separately to the lower regions of Pātāla.
Having consoled the thirty gods, Viṣṇu, worshipped by the thirty gods, / vanished right there while all of them were watching.
Even Laṅkā became deserted, O best of kings, and was given to Vaiśravaṇa; / having belonged to Viśravas himself, it was taken by force by Rāvaṇa.
Having slain Rāvaṇa, it was given to Vibhīṣaṇa by you. / O Rāma, you are Viṣṇu born here for the destruction of the rakshasas.

yenātmā vijitastena vijiteyaṃ vasundharā .. 12 ..
rājño'vijitacittasya paracakrajayaḥ kutaḥ..
na cakasya jayaṃ kartuṃ śaknotyavijitendriyaḥ..13..
1.180.d:
त्वयैव युद्धे निहता ये तु मातुलसङ्कटाः ॥
पौलस्त्यराक्षसा ये तु ते हताः सम्मतं त्वया ॥ 7 ॥
हन्ता न विद्यते राम रक्षसां केशवं विना ॥।
दृष्टोऽस्मि भाषितश्चेति प्रययौ स यथागतम् ॥ 8 ॥
॥ नाडायन उवाच ॥
एवमुक्त्वा ततोऽगस्त्यो यथागतमरिन्दम ॥
तस्माद्युद्धं न मे राजन्नद्य वै तव रोचते ॥ 9 ॥
उत्साहशक्त्या सम्पन्नो मन्त्रशक्त्या च राघवः ॥
प्रभुशक्त्या तथा युक्तो देवशक्त्या तथैव च ॥ 1.218.10 ॥
साधुसाध्येषु कार्येषु कः कुर्याद्विग्रहं बुधः ॥
केवलं कोपमास्थाय विग्रहं नृपदोषदम् ॥ .1 ॥
कामक्रोधौ जितौ येन तेनात्मा विजितस्तथा ॥
येनात्मा विजितस्तेन विजितेयं वसुन्धरा ॥ 12 ॥
राज्ञोऽविजितचित्तस्य परचक्रजयः कुतः॥
न चकस्य जयं कर्तुं शक्नोत्यविजितेन्द्रियः॥13॥
1.180.m:
Indeed, by you alone were slain in battle those who were a danger through their maternal uncles; / those who were the Paulastya rakshasas have been slain by you as acknowledged.
There is no slayer of the rakshasas other than Keśava, O Rāma. / "I have seen and spoken [with you]," saying this, he departed as he had come.
Nāḍāyana said: / Having spoken thus, Agastya then departed as he had come, O subduer of foes. / Therefore, O king, battle today does not please me for you.
Rāghava is endowed with the power of energy and the power of counsel; / he is likewise possessed of the power of majesty and of divine power.
What wise man would wage war over matters that can be accomplished through conciliation, / resorting solely to anger—a war that brings ruin to a king?
He by whom desire and anger are conquered, by him the self is conquered; / he by whom the self is conquered, by him this earth is conquered.
For a king whose mind is unconquered, whence can come victory over enemy forces? / One whose senses are unconquered cannot achieve the conquest of anyone.

1.180.s:
nāvajñā kasyacitkāryā'balo vā bahumanyate ..
nityaṃ loke hi dṛśyante śaktebhyaḥ śaktimattarāḥ .. 14 ..
yathāśakti cikīrṣanti yathāśakti ca kurvate ..
na kaścidavamanyante narāḥ paṇḍitabuddhayaḥ .. 15 ..

yaścādhanaḥ kāmayate yaśca kupyatyanīśvaraḥ .. 16 ..

prabhuśca kṣamayā yukto daridraśca pradānavān .. 17 ..
kaḥ kuryāddurbale krodhaṃ svabhāvādeva nirjite ..
balavatyapi kaḥ krodhaṃ kuryātprāṇaharaṃ naraḥ .. 18 ..
apahārapravṛttasya kopastejasvitocyate ..

trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanamātmanaḥ ..
kāmaḥ krodhastathā lobhastasmādetattrayaṃ tyajet..1.218.20..
1.180.d:
नावज्ञा कस्यचित्कार्याऽबलो वा बहुमन्यते ॥
नित्यं लोके हि दृश्यन्ते शक्तेभ्यः शक्तिमत्तराः ॥ 14 ॥
यथाशक्ति चिकीर्षन्ति यथाशक्ति च कुर्वते ॥
न कश्चिदवमन्यन्ते नराः पण्डितबुद्धयः ॥ 15 ॥
द्वाविमौ कण्टकौ तीक्ष्णौ शरीरपरिशोषणौ ॥
यश्चाधनः कामयते यश्च कुप्यत्यनीश्वरः ॥ 16 ॥
द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके स्वर्गस्योपरि तिष्ठतः ॥
प्रभुश्च क्षमया युक्तो दरिद्रश्च प्रदानवान् ॥ 17 ॥
कः कुर्याद्दुर्बले क्रोधं स्वभावादेव निर्जिते ॥
बलवत्यपि कः क्रोधं कुर्यात्प्राणहरं नरः ॥ 18 ॥
अपहारप्रवृत्तस्य कोपस्तेजस्वितोच्यते ॥
यस्मात्तस्माद्बुधैः कोपः कोपं कृत्वा विनिर्जितः ॥19॥
त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः ॥
कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत्॥1.218.20॥
1.180.m:
Contempt must not be shown to anyone, whether weak or highly esteemed; / for in this world, stronger persons are always seen than the strong.
Men of wise intellect desire to act according to their ability and act according to their ability; / they hold no one in contempt.
These two are sharp thorns that dry up the body: / he who, being penniless, desires, and he who, being powerless, becomes angry.
These two men in this world stand above heaven: / a master endowed with forbearance, and a poor man who is generous.
Who would direct anger toward a weak person who is subdued by his very nature? / And toward a strong person, what man would direct anger that destroys his own life?
Anger toward one engaged in seizing [what is right] is called spiritedness; / therefore, anger has been subdued by the wise by becoming angry at anger.
Threefold is this gate of hell that brings ruin to the self: / desire, anger, and greed; therefore, one should abandon these three.

1.180.s:
anubandhaṃ ca saṃprekṣya vipākaṃ caiva karmaṇām ..
utthānamātmanaścaiva tataḥ karmasamārabhet .. 21 ..

śriyaṃ hyavinayo hanti jarārūpamivottamam .. 22 ..

aviṣahyatamaṃ hatvā rāvaṇaṃ lokarāvaṇam ..

dhanādhipo'dyāpi viśāla kīrtiḥ karoti rājyaṃ kṣaṇadācarāṇām..24..
1.219
.. śailūṣa uvāca .. ..
kathaṃ vaiśravaṇe dattā purā laṅkā dvijottama ..
kathaṃ cāpahatā tasya rāvaṇena mahātmanā .. 1 ..
caritaṃ rāvaṇasyāhaṃ śrotumicchāmi tattvataḥ ..
trailokyaṃ vijitaṃ yena tapasā pauruṣeṇa ca .. 2 ..
1.180.d:
अनुबन्धं च संप्रेक्ष्य विपाकं चैव कर्मणाम् ॥
उत्थानमात्मनश्चैव ततः कर्मसमारभेत् ॥ 21 ॥
न राज्यं लब्धमित्येवं वर्तितव्यं च साम्प्रतम् ॥
श्रियं ह्यविनयो हन्ति जरारूपमिवोत्तमम् ॥ 22 ॥
त्यक्त्वा जनपदे वासं याहि राजन्हिमाचलम् ॥
अविषह्यतमं हत्वा रावणं लोकरावणम् ॥
लङ्कां त्यक्त्वा धनाध्यक्षं पश्य कैलासमाश्रितम् ॥ 23 ॥
स रावणो राघवसायकार्त्तस्त्यक्त्वा श्रियं भूमिपते विपन्नः ॥
धनाधिपोऽद्यापि विशाल कीर्तिः करोति राज्यं क्षणदाचराणाम्॥24॥
1.219
॥ शैलूष उवाच ॥ ॥
कथं वैश्रवणे दत्ता पुरा लङ्का द्विजोत्तम ॥
कथं चापहता तस्य रावणेन महात्मना ॥ 1 ॥
चरितं रावणस्याहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः ॥
त्रैलोक्यं विजितं येन तपसा पौरुषेण च ॥ 2 ॥
1.180.m:
Considering the consequence and the fruition of deeds, / as well as one's own enterprise, one should then undertake action.
One should not behave [carelessly] merely thinking that kingship has been acquired; / for lack of discipline destroys fortune, just as old age destroys excellent beauty.
Leaving your dwelling among the inhabited lands, go, O king, to the Himālayas. / Having slain Rāvaṇa, the most unbearable one who made the worlds weep, / see the lord of wealth, who abandoned Laṅkā and took refuge on Kailāsa.
That Rāvaṇa, afflicted by the arrows of Rāghava, abandoned his royal fortune and perished, O lord of the earth; / while the lord of wealth, whose fame is vast, even today rules over the night-wanderers.
1.219
Śailūṣa said:
How was Laṅkā given of old to Vaiśravaṇa, O best of the twice-born? / And how was it wrested from him by the high-souled Rāvaṇa?
I wish to hear truly the life of Rāvaṇa, / by whom the three worlds were conquered through his ascetic power and manly strength.

1.180.d:
॥ नाडायन उवाच ॥ ॥
ब्रह्मणो मानसः पुत्रः पुलस्त्यो विदितस्तथा ॥
तस्यासीद्विश्रवा नाम पुत्रस्त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतः ॥ 3 ॥
पौत्री बृहस्पतेः पत्नी भरद्वाजसुता शुभा ॥
बभूव तस्य राजेन्द्र नाम्ना वै देववर्णिनी ॥ 4 ॥
तस्यां स जनयामास पुत्रं वैश्रवणं प्रभुम् ॥
आराधितः सुतपसा प्रादात्तस्य पितामहः ॥ 5 ॥
यक्षेशत्वं धनेशत्वं लोकपालत्वमेव च ॥
पुष्पकं च तथा यानं कामगं कामरूपिणम् ॥ 6 ॥
पुत्रं लब्धवरं राजन्विश्रवा अभ्यभाषत ॥
त्रिकूटे पर्वतश्रेष्ठे निर्मिता विश्वकर्मणा ॥ 7 ॥
लङ्का नाम पुरी रम्या देवराजकृते पुरा ॥
हृत्वा तां देवराजस्य सुकेशतनयैः पुरा ॥ 8 ॥
आयासिता महाराज तेषां ज्येष्ठं तु मालिनम् ॥
निपात्य वासुदेवेन ते तु विद्रावितास्ततः ॥ 9 ॥
पातालतलमाश्रित्य ते वसन्तीह निर्भयाः ॥ 1.219.10 ॥
1.180.m:
Nāḍāyana said:
Pulastya is known as the mind-born son of Brahmā; / his son was Viśravas, renowned throughout the three worlds.
Bṛhaspati's granddaughter and Bharadvāja's auspicious daughter / became his wife, O ruler of kings, named indeed Devavarṇinī.
Upon her he fathered a lordly son, Vaiśravaṇa. / Propitiated by his excellent austerities, the Grandfather granted him
the lordship over the Yakṣas, the lordship over wealth, and guardianship of the world, / as well as the Puṣpaka aerial car, which moves at will and changes its shape at will.
To his son who had obtained the boons, O king, Viśravas spoke: / 'Constructed by Viśvakarman on Trikūṭa, the foremost of mountains,
was the delightful city named Laṅkā, built of old for the sake of the king of the gods. / Having stolen it of old from the king of the gods, the sons of Sukeśa
caused distress [to the gods], O great king; but after Vāsudeva / struck down Mālin, the eldest among them, they were put to flight from there.
Having taken refuge in the netherworld, they live here free from fear. 1.219.10

1.180.s:
tāṃ tvaṃ laṅkāṃ samāsādya vasa yakṣasamanvitaḥ ..
dharmeṇa pālayanrājyaṃ satataṃ rākṣaseśvara .. 11 ..
dharme te dīyatāṃ buddhiḥ sarvāvasthasya sarvadā ..
dharmādarthaśca kāmaśca dharmamūlamidaṃ jagat .. 12 ..
śrutvā piturvākyamadīnasattvo laṅkāṃ samāsādya dhanādhināthaḥ ..
dharmeṇa lokaṃ sa tu rañjayānaścakāra rājyaṃ kṣaṇadācarāṇām .. 13 ..
1.220
.. nāḍāyana uvāca .. ..
etasminneva kāle tu sumālī vasudhātalam ..
cacārādāya tanayāṃ kaikasīṃ nāma nāmataḥ .. 1 ..
caransa vasudhāṃ sphītāṃ dadarśātha narādhipam ..
puṣpakaṃ yānamārūḍhaṃ śriyā paramayā yutam .. 2 ..
taṃ dṛṣṭvā kaikasīṃ vākyaṃ covāca rajanīcaraḥ ..
putri pradānakālaste na kaścittvāṃ vṛṇoti mām .. 3 ..
aprārthitapradānaṃ ca dharṣaṇābhayaśaṅkayā ..
na karomi viśālākṣi tavārthaṃ varavarṇini .. 4 ..
1.180.d:
तां त्वं लङ्कां समासाद्य वस यक्षसमन्वितः ॥
धर्मेण पालयन्राज्यं सततं राक्षसेश्वर ॥ 11 ॥
धर्मे ते दीयतां बुद्धिः सर्वावस्थस्य सर्वदा ॥
धर्मादर्थश्च कामश्च धर्ममूलमिदं जगत् ॥ 12 ॥
श्रुत्वा पितुर्वाक्यमदीनसत्त्वो लङ्कां समासाद्य धनाधिनाथः ॥
धर्मेण लोकं स तु रञ्जयानश्चकार राज्यं क्षणदाचराणाम् ॥ 13 ॥
1.220
॥ नाडायन उवाच ॥ ॥
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु सुमाली वसुधातलम् ॥
चचारादाय तनयां कैकसीं नाम नामतः ॥ 1 ॥
चरन्स वसुधां स्फीतां ददर्शाथ नराधिपम् ॥
पुष्पकं यानमारूढं श्रिया परमया युतम् ॥ 2 ॥
तं दृष्ट्वा कैकसीं वाक्यं चोवाच रजनीचरः ॥
पुत्रि प्रदानकालस्ते न कश्चित्त्वां वृणोति माम् ॥ 3 ॥
अप्रार्थितप्रदानं च धर्षणाभयशङ्कया ॥
न करोमि विशालाक्षि तवार्थं वरवर्णिनि ॥ 4 ॥
1.180.m:
Proceeding to that Laṅkā, dwell there accompanied by the Yakṣas, / ruling the kingdom according to dharma constantly, O lord of rākṣasas.
Let your mind be set on dharma in every condition at all times. / From dharma arise wealth and pleasure; this world is rooted in dharma.'
Hearing his father's words, the lord of wealth, whose courage was undaunted, reached Laṅkā, / and delighting the world with dharma, he ruled over the night-wanderers.
1.220
Nāḍāyana said:
At that very time, Sumālī roamed the surface of the earth, / taking with him his daughter, Kaikasī by name.
As he wandered over the thriving earth, he saw the ruler of men / mounted on the Puṣpaka car, endowed with supreme splendour.
Seeing him, the night-wanderer spoke these words to Kaikasī: / 'Daughter, the time has come to give you away, yet no one chooses you from me.
Nor do I offer you unasked, for fear of rejection and insult, / for your sake, O large-eyed girl of excellent complexion.

1.180.s:
kaṣṭaṃ kanyāpitṛtvaṃ hi narāṇāṃ mānakāṅkṣiṇām ..
dhruvaṃ kanyāpitṛtvaṃ hi śakrasyāpi pradharṣaṇam .. 5 ..
mātuḥ kulaṃ pitṛkulaṃ yatra kanyā pradīyate ..
kulatrayaṃ saṃśayitaṃ kanyā kṛtveha tiṣṭhati .. 6 ..
tenāhaṃ tvāṃ na dāsyāmi sā tvaṃ gaccha svayaṃ śubhe ..
bhartāraṃ varayasvāśu muniṃ viśravasaṃ vibhum .. 7 ..
yataḥ so'yaṃ dhanādhyakṣaḥ śriyā paramayā yutaḥ ..
tādṛśaṃ tanayaṃ tasmājjanayiṣyasi bhāmini .. 8 ..
jagāma kaikasī rājaṃstato viśravasaṃ munim ..
raudre muhūrte saṃprāpte sandhyāyāṃ nṛpasattama .. 9 ..
