vijñātastvadabhiprāyo mayādya varavarṇini .. 11 ..
1.180.d:
कष्टं कन्यापितृत्वं हि नराणां मानकाङ्क्षिणाम् ॥
ध्रुवं कन्यापितृत्वं हि शक्रस्यापि प्रधर्षणम् ॥ 5 ॥
मातुः कुलं पितृकुलं यत्र कन्या प्रदीयते ॥
कुलत्रयं संशयितं कन्या कृत्वेह तिष्ठति ॥ 6 ॥
तेनाहं त्वां न दास्यामि सा त्वं गच्छ स्वयं शुभे ॥
भर्तारं वरयस्वाशु मुनिं विश्रवसं विभुम् ॥ 7 ॥
यतः सोऽयं धनाध्यक्षः श्रिया परमया युतः ॥
तादृशं तनयं तस्माज्जनयिष्यसि भामिनि ॥ 8 ॥
जगाम कैकसी राजंस्ततो विश्रवसं मुनिम् ॥
रौद्रे मुहूर्ते संप्राप्ते सन्ध्यायां नृपसत्तम ॥ 9 ॥
साभिवन्द्य ततः पादौ तस्य विश्रवसो मुनेः ॥
बभूव पुरतस्तन्वी व्रीडमानेव लज्जया ॥ 1.220.10 ॥
उवाच तां मुनिः प्रह्वां कैकसीं चारुहासिनीम् ॥
विज्ञातस्त्वदभिप्रायो मयाद्य वरवर्णिनि ॥ 11 ॥
1.180.m:
Painful indeed is fatherhood of a daughter for men who desire honour; / fatherhood of a daughter is certainly a humiliation even for Śakra.
The mother's family, the father's family, and that to which the maiden is given— / a maiden stands here placing all three families in jeopardy.
Therefore I shall not give you away; go yourself, O auspicious one, / and swiftly choose as your husband the sage, the powerful Viśravas.
Since this lord of wealth is endowed with supreme splendour, / you will bear from him a son of such a kind, O beautiful lady.'
Kaikasī then went, O king, to the sage Viśravas / at a dreadful hour, when twilight had arrived, O best of kings.
Having paid homage to the feet of that sage Viśravas, / the slender woman stood before him, as if ashamed with modesty. 1.220.10
The sage spoke to that Kaikasī, who was bowed low and had a charming smile: / 'Your intention has been understood by me today, O fair-complexioned one.

1.180.s:
putrārthaṃ tvamanuprāptā matsamīpamanindite ..
raudre kāle yathā prāptā tādṛśaṃ janayiṣyasi .. 12 ..
evamastvityathoktā sā tatrovāsa sukhaṃ tadā ..
tataḥ kālena sā putraṃ janayāmāsa bhāminī .. 13 ..
daśāsyaṃ viṃśatibhujamekadehaṃ mahābalam ..
nāma tasya pitā cakre daśagrīveti buddhimān .. 14 ..
tato dvitīyaṃ tanayaṃ mahākāyaṃ suṣāva sā ..
kumbhakarṇeti tasyāpi nāma cakre tadā pitā .. 15 ..
tatra śūrpaṇakhāṃ kanyāṃ janayāmāsa sā tadā ..
tataḥ kadācitsā putraṃ kaikasī jyeṣṭhamabravīt .. 16 ..
darśayantī dhanādhyakṣaṃ savrīḍeva parantapa ..
paśya svīyāgrajasyāsya śriyaṃ bhrāturdaśānana .. 17 ..
sa tvaṃ yatnamathāsthāya bhava vaiśravaṇopamaḥ ..
evamuktastu gokarṇaṃ prayayau bhrātṛbhiḥ saha .. 18 ..
śīrṇaparṇāśanastatra cakāra sumahattapaḥ ..
pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu śiraśchitvā daśānanaḥ .. 19 ..
1.180.d:
पुत्रार्थं त्वमनुप्राप्ता मत्समीपमनिन्दिते ॥
रौद्रे काले यथा प्राप्ता तादृशं जनयिष्यसि ॥ 12 ॥
एवमस्त्वित्यथोक्ता सा तत्रोवास सुखं तदा ॥
ततः कालेन सा पुत्रं जनयामास भामिनी ॥ 13 ॥
दशास्यं विंशतिभुजमेकदेहं महाबलम् ॥
नाम तस्य पिता चक्रे दशग्रीवेति बुद्धिमान् ॥ 14 ॥
ततो द्वितीयं तनयं महाकायं सुषाव सा ॥
कुम्भकर्णेति तस्यापि नाम चक्रे तदा पिता ॥ 15 ॥
तत्र शूर्पणखां कन्यां जनयामास सा तदा ॥
ततः कदाचित्सा पुत्रं कैकसी ज्येष्ठमब्रवीत् ॥ 16 ॥
दर्शयन्ती धनाध्यक्षं सव्रीडेव परन्तप ॥
पश्य स्वीयाग्रजस्यास्य श्रियं भ्रातुर्दशानन ॥ 17 ॥
स त्वं यत्नमथास्थाय भव वैश्रवणोपमः ॥
एवमुक्तस्तु गोकर्णं प्रययौ भ्रातृभिः सह ॥ 18 ॥
शीर्णपर्णाशनस्तत्र चकार सुमहत्तपः ॥
पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु शिरश्छित्वा दशाननः ॥ 19 ॥
1.180.m:
You have come to my presence for the sake of a son, O blameless lady; / as you have approached at a dreadful time, such a son shall you bring forth.'
Told 'So be it,' she then dwelt there happily. / Then, in time, that beautiful woman gave birth to a son:
ten-faced, twenty-armed, with a single body, exceedingly strong. / His wise father gave him the name Daśagrīva.
Then she brought forth a second son, possessing a massive body; / his father gave him the name Kumbhakarṇa at that time.
Then she also gave birth to a daughter, Śūrpaṇakhā. / Thereafter, at one time, Kaikasī said to her eldest son,
pointing out the lord of wealth, as if with bashfulness, O scorcher of foes: / 'Behold the splendour of your elder brother, O ten-faced one.
Therefore, exert yourself and become equal to Vaiśravaṇa.' / Thus addressed, he departed for Gokarṇa along with his brothers.
Subsisting on fallen leaves, he performed very severe asceticism there. / When a thousand years were completed, the ten-faced one, cutting off a head,

1.180.s:
juhāvāgnau mahābhāga ekaikaṃ tapasā kṛśaḥ ..
grīṣme pañcatapā bhūtvā varṣāsvākāśaśāyikaḥ .. 1.220.20 ..
ārdravāsaśca śiśire kumbhakarṇo'pyatapyata ..
vibhīṣaṇastataḥ kāle ṣaṣṭhe ṣaṣṭhe phalāśanaḥ .. 21 ..
paricaryāṃ tadā teṣāṃ cakre śūrpaṇakhā svasā ..
daśavarṣasahasrānte tadā kāle daśānanaḥ .. 22 ..
daśamaṃ mastakaṃ vahnau juhūṣati yadā prabho ..
tatastaṃ deśamāgamya brahmā vacanamabravīt .. 23 ..
.. brahmovāca ..
varaṃ varaya bhadrante parituṣṭo'smi putraka ..
tapasā te sutaptena sattvena vipulena ca .. 24 ..
.. nāḍāyana uvāca ..
devādīni sa bhūtāni kīrtayāmāsa rākṣasaḥ ..
sarvāṇyevāviśeṣeṇa varjayitvā tu mānuṣam .. 25 ..
saṃkīrtya tebhyo'vadhyatvaṃ varayāmāsa bhūmipa ..
trailokyaviṣayaṃ caiva tacca tasya dadau prabhuḥ .. 26 ..
1.180.d:
जुहावाग्नौ महाभाग एकैकं तपसा कृशः ॥
ग्रीष्मे पञ्चतपा भूत्वा वर्षास्वाकाशशायिकः ॥ 1.220.20 ॥
आर्द्रवासश्च शिशिरे कुम्भकर्णोऽप्यतप्यत ॥
विभीषणस्ततः काले षष्ठे षष्ठे फलाशनः ॥ 21 ॥
परिचर्यां तदा तेषां चक्रे शूर्पणखा स्वसा ॥
दशवर्षसहस्रान्ते तदा काले दशाननः ॥ 22 ॥
दशमं मस्तकं वह्नौ जुहूषति यदा प्रभो ॥
ततस्तं देशमागम्य ब्रह्मा वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 23 ॥
॥ ब्रह्मोवाच ॥
वरं वरय भद्रन्ते परितुष्टोऽस्मि पुत्रक ॥
तपसा ते सुतप्तेन सत्त्वेन विपुलेन च ॥ 24 ॥
॥ नाडायन उवाच ॥
देवादीनि स भूतानि कीर्तयामास राक्षसः ॥
सर्वाण्येवाविशेषेण वर्जयित्वा तु मानुषम् ॥ 25 ॥
संकीर्त्य तेभ्योऽवध्यत्वं वरयामास भूमिप ॥
त्रैलोक्यविषयं चैव तच्च तस्य ददौ प्रभुः ॥ 26 ॥
1.180.m:
sacrificed them one by one into the fire, emaciated by austerities, O highly fortunate one. / Kumbhakarṇa also practised austerities, exposing himself to the five fires in summer, sleeping in the open in the rains,
and wearing wet clothes in winter. / Then Vibhīṣaṇa ate fruit only at every sixth mealtime.
Their sister Śūrpaṇakhā attended upon them then. / Then, at the end of ten thousand years, when the ten-faced one
wished to sacrifice his tenth head into the fire, O lord, / Brahmā, arriving at that place, spoke these words:
Brahmā said:
'Choose a boon, may good betide you; I am well pleased, my son, / with your well-performed austerity and your immense fortitude.'
Nāḍāyana said:
The rākṣasa enumerated all beings beginning with the gods, / completely without exception, leaving out only human beings.
Having named them, he asked for invulnerability against them, O ruler of the earth, / and dominion over the three worlds; and the Lord granted that to him.

1.180.s:
chandayitvā vareṇā'tha daśagrīvaṃ niśācaram ..
nyastvā sarasvatīṃ vaktre kumbhakarṇaṃ sa rākṣasam .. 27 ..
vareṇacchandayāmāsa tadāgatya vibhīṣaṇam ..
sa vavre nityakālaṃ tu matiṃ dharme sanātanīm ..28..
tena tasya tadā tuṣṭastvamaratvaṃ dadau prabhuḥ ..
vareṇacchandayitvā tānbrahmā svabhavanaṃ gataḥ.. 29..
varalabdhaṃ daśagrīvaṃ jñātvā rakṣogaṇastadā ..
pātālāttu viniṣkramya mahārājye'bhyaṣecayat ..1.220.30..
sa tu rājyaṃ tadā labdhvā preṣayāmāsa rākṣasān ..
kuberāya tadā dūtaṃ prahasta nāma nāmataḥ ..31..
rākṣasānāmadhīvāso laṅkeyaṃ nirmitā purā ..
tāṃ tyajasva dhanādhyakṣa sāmnaiva mama mā ciram.. 32 ..
1.180.d:
छन्दयित्वा वरेणाऽथ दशग्रीवं निशाचरम् ॥
न्यस्त्वा सरस्वतीं वक्त्रे कुम्भकर्णं स राक्षसम् ॥ 27 ॥
वरेणच्छन्दयामास तदागत्य विभीषणम् ॥
स वव्रे नित्यकालं तु मतिं धर्मे सनातनीम् ॥28॥
तेन तस्य तदा तुष्टस्त्वमरत्वं ददौ प्रभुः ॥
वरेणच्छन्दयित्वा तान्ब्रह्मा स्वभवनं गतः॥ 29॥
वरलब्धं दशग्रीवं ज्ञात्वा रक्षोगणस्तदा ॥
पातालात्तु विनिष्क्रम्य महाराज्येऽभ्यषेचयत् ॥1.220.30॥
स तु राज्यं तदा लब्ध्वा प्रेषयामास राक्षसान् ॥
कुबेराय तदा दूतं प्रहस्त नाम नामतः ॥31॥
राक्षसानामधीवासो लङ्केयं निर्मिता पुरा ॥
तां त्यजस्व धनाध्यक्ष साम्नैव मम मा चिरम्॥ 32 ॥
1.180.m:
Then, having gratified the night-roamer Daśagrīva with a boon, / [and] having placed Sarasvatī in the mouth of the rakshasa Kumbhakarṇa,
he came and gratified Vibhīṣaṇa with a boon. / He chose an eternal mind ever set on dharma.
Pleased with that, the Lord then gave him immortality. / Having gratified them with boons, Brahmā went to his own abode.
Knowing that Daśagrīva had obtained a boon, the hosts of rakshasas then / emerged from Pātāla and consecrated him in the great sovereignty.
Having obtained the kingdom, he then sent the rakshasas, / [and] then an envoy named Prahasta to Kubera:
‘This Laṅkā was constructed in the past as the dwelling of the rakshasas. / Relinquish it through peaceful conciliation alone to me, O superintendent of wealth, without delay!’

1.180.s:
prahastavacanaṃ śrutvā dhanādhyakṣo mahāmatiḥ ..
daśagrīvaṃ varonmattaṃ jñātvā tatyāja tāṃ purīm ..33..
1.180.d:
प्रहस्तवचनं श्रुत्वा धनाध्यक्षो महामतिः ॥
दशग्रीवं वरोन्मत्तं ज्ञात्वा तत्याज तां पुरीम् ॥33॥
1.180.m: Hearing Prahasta’s words, the wise superintendent of wealth, / knowing that Daśagrīva was maddened by the boons, abandoned that city.

1.180.s:
kailāsaṃ parvataṃ gatvā tadā cakre purīṃ śubhām ..
alakāṃ nāma rājendra yatrāste sa sukhī sadā ..34..
1.180.d:
कैलासं पर्वतं गत्वा तदा चक्रे पुरीं शुभाम् ॥
अलकां नाम राजेन्द्र यत्रास्ते स सुखी सदा ॥34॥
1.180.m: Going to Mount Kailāsa, he then built an auspicious city / named Alakā, O king of kings, where he always dwells in happiness.

1.180.s:
daśagrīvo mahārāja trilokavijayaṃ tathā ..
cakre laṅkāmathāsādya varadānātsvayambhuvaḥ ..35..
1.180.d:
दशग्रीवो महाराज त्रिलोकविजयं तथा ॥
चक्रे लङ्कामथासाद्य वरदानात्स्वयम्भुवः ॥35॥
1.180.m: Then Daśagrīva, O great king, having reached Laṅkā, / accomplished the conquest of the three worlds by virtue of the boon of the Self-born.

1.180.s:
mandodarīṃ nāma bhāryāṃ tadā lebhe mayātmajām ..
tasyāṃ sa janayāmāsa meghanādaṃ tathā sutam .. 36 ..
1.180.d:
मन्दोदरीं नाम भार्यां तदा लेभे मयात्मजाम् ॥
तस्यां स जनयामास मेघनादं तथा सुतम् ॥ 36 ॥
1.180.m: He then obtained a wife named Mandodarī, the daughter of Maya; / on her he fathered a son, Meghanāda.

1.180.s:
trilokavijayī śrīmāndevabrāhmaṇakaṇṭakaḥ ..
nihataḥ sa tu kālena viṣṇunā nararūpiṇā.. 37 ..
1.180.d:
त्रिलोकविजयी श्रीमान्देवब्राह्मणकण्टकः ॥
निहतः स तु कालेन विष्णुना नररूपिणा॥ 37 ॥
1.180.m: The glorious conqueror of the three worlds, a thorn to gods and brahmins, / was in time slain by Viṣṇu in human form,

1.180.s:
rāghaveṇa mahārāja rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā ..
laṅkāṃ tyaktvā dhanādhyakṣaḥ kailāse parvatottame .. 38 ..
1.180.d:
राघवेण महाराज रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा ॥
लङ्कां त्यक्त्वा धनाध्यक्षः कैलासे पर्वतोत्तमे ॥ 38 ॥
1.180.m: by the descendant of Raghu, Rāma of untiring deeds, O great king. / Having abandoned Laṅkā, the superintendent of wealth, on Kailāsa, the foremost of mountains,

1.180.s:
adyāpi pālayannāste rājyaṃ nihatakaṇṭakam..
tasmāttvamapi rājendra tyaktvā deśamimaṃ svayam..
himavantamathāsādya vasa vaiśravaṇopamaḥ ..39..
1.180.d:
अद्यापि पालयन्नास्ते राज्यं निहतकण्टकम्॥
तस्मात्त्वमपि राजेन्द्र त्यक्त्वा देशमिमं स्वयम्॥
हिमवन्तमथासाद्य वस वैश्रवणोपमः ॥39॥
1.180.m: dwells even today protecting his kingdom, its thorns removed. / Therefore, O king of kings, you too should personally abandon this region, / and reaching the Himavat, dwell like Vaiśravaṇa.

1.180.s:
tasmānna kāryaṃ bharatena vairaṃ mahābalāstrā raghavaḥ pratītāḥ..
prasīda jīvantu saputrapautrāḥ putrāstaveme tuhinādrisaṃsthāḥ ..1.220.40..
1.180.d:
तस्मान्न कार्यं भरतेन वैरं महाबलास्त्रा रघवः प्रतीताः॥
प्रसीद जीवन्तु सपुत्रपौत्राः पुत्रास्तवेमे तुहिनाद्रिसंस्थाः ॥1.220.40॥
1.180.m: Therefore enmity should not be made with Bharata; the descendants of Raghu are famed for weapons of great might. / Be gracious! Let these sons of yours, dwelling on the snow-mountain, live with their sons and grandsons!’

1.181.s:
śailūṣa uvāca ..
śrotumicchāmyahaṃ tasya daśagrīvasya rakṣasaḥ ..
trilokavijayaṃ brahmaṃstatra me saṃśayo mahān .. 1 ..
1.181.d:
शैलूष उवाच ॥
श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं तस्य दशग्रीवस्य रक्षसः ॥
त्रिलोकविजयं ब्रह्मंस्तत्र मे संशयो महान् ॥ 1 ॥
1.181.m: Śailūṣa said: / ‘I wish to hear of the conquest of the three worlds by that rakshasa Daśagrīva, / O holy one; regarding that, I have a great doubt.’

1.181.s:
nāḍāyana uvāca ..
varapradānātsaṃmatto daśagrīvo niśācaraḥ ..
devagandharvadaityānāṃ nāgendroragarakṣamām..2..
1.181.d:
नाडायन उवाच ॥
वरप्रदानात्संमत्तो दशग्रीवो निशाचरः ॥
देवगन्धर्वदैत्यानां नागेन्द्रोरगरक्षमाम्॥2॥
1.181.m: Nāḍāyana said: / ‘Maddened by the grant of boons, the night-roamer Daśagrīva / [attacked] the gods, gandharvas, daityas, lords of nāgas, uragas, and rakshasas.

1.181.s:
ākramyā'kramya ratnāni sa jahāra tadā balāt ..
patnyaśca rājaśārdūla tadā duhitaraḥ śubhāḥ.. 3 ..
1.181.d:
आक्रम्याऽक्रम्य रत्नानि स जहार तदा बलात् ॥
पत्न्यश्च राजशार्दूल तदा दुहितरः शुभाः॥ 3 ॥
1.181.m: Attacking again and again, he then seized their jewels by force, / and their wives, O tiger among kings, and their lovely daughters.

1.181.s:
narendrāndharmasaṃsaktānbrāhmaṇāṃśca jighāṃsati ..
ayodhyāvāsinaṃ vīramanaraṇyaṃ ca jaghnivān .. 4 ..
1.181.d:
नरेन्द्रान्धर्मसंसक्तान्ब्राह्मणांश्च जिघांसति ॥
अयोध्यावासिनं वीरमनरण्यं च जघ्निवान् ॥ 4 ॥
1.181.m: He sought to kill kings devoted to dharma, and brahmins; / and he slew the heroic Anaraṇya, who dwelt in Ayodhyā.

1.181.s:
saṃgrāme nihatastena daśagrīvaṃ sa śaptavān ..
utpatsyati kule nīca puruṣo mama vīryavān .. 5 ..
1.181.d:
संग्रामे निहतस्तेन दशग्रीवं स शप्तवान् ॥
उत्पत्स्यति कुले नीच पुरुषो मम वीर्यवान् ॥ 5 ॥
1.181.m: Slain by him in battle, he cursed Daśagrīva: / ‘A mighty man will be born in my lineage, O vile one,

1.181.s:
yastavādāsyati prāṇānsamare samarapriya ..
yuyudhe ca tathā rājñā māṃdhātrā raṇaśālinā .. 6 ..
1.181.d:
यस्तवादास्यति प्राणान्समरे समरप्रिय ॥
युयुधे च तथा राज्ञा मांधात्रा रणशालिना ॥ 6 ॥
1.181.m: who will take your life in battle, O you who delight in war!’ / And he likewise fought with King Māndhātṛ, who was distinguished in battle.

1.181.s:
tatrainaṃ vārayāmāsa nārado munisattamaḥ ..
mayūrasya tato yajñe bhakṣayāmāsa vai dvijān .. 7 ..
1.181.d:
तत्रैनं वारयामास नारदो मुनिसत्तमः ॥
मयूरस्य ततो यज्ञे भक्षयामास वै द्विजान् ॥ 7 ॥
1.181.m: There Nārada, the best of sages, checked him. / Then, at the sacrifice of Marutta, he devoured the twice-born.

1.181.s:
indro mayūrarūpeṇa tasmādyajñādapākramat ..
mayūrasya varaṃ prādānmeghe varṣati sarvadā .. 8 ..
1.181.d:
इन्द्रो मयूररूपेण तस्माद्यज्ञादपाक्रमत् ॥
मयूरस्य वरं प्रादान्मेघे वर्षति सर्वदा ॥ 8 ॥
1.181.m: Indra slipped away from that sacrifice in the form of a peacock; / he granted a boon to the peacock: ‘Whenever a cloud rains,

1.181.s:
gamiṣyasyatulāṃ prītiṃ mama netragaṇākṛtim ..
dhārayiṣyasi loke'sminkalāpaṃ sumanoharam .. 9 ..
1.181.d:
गमिष्यस्यतुलां प्रीतिं मम नेत्रगणाकृतिम् ॥
धारयिष्यसि लोकेऽस्मिन्कलापं सुमनोहरम् ॥ 9 ॥
1.181.m: you will experience peerless joy; / you will bear in this world a very captivating tail-plumage in the likeness of my multitude of eyes.’

1.181.s:
kṛkalāsasya rūpeṇa dhanādhyakṣo vyapākramat ..
varṇaṃ tasya suvarṇābhaṃ sadravyaṃ ca tathā śiraḥ .. 1.221.10 ..
1.181.d:
कृकलासस्य रूपेण धनाध्यक्षो व्यपाक्रमत् ॥
वर्णं तस्य सुवर्णाभं सद्रव्यं च तथा शिरः ॥ 1.221.10 ॥
1.181.m: The superintendent of wealth slipped away in the form of a chameleon; / he granted him a colour like gold and a head endowed with treasure;

1.181.s:
prādāddvayamameyātmā rājarājena dānava ..
varuṇaśca tadā rājanhaṃsarūpeṇa nirgataḥ .. 11 ..
1.181.d:
प्रादाद्द्वयममेयात्मा राजराजेन दानव ॥
वरुणश्च तदा राजन्हंसरूपेण निर्गतः ॥ 11 ॥
1.181.m: the king of kings of immeasurable soul granted both, O Danu's son. / And Varuṇa, O king, then departed in the form of a swan.

1.181.s:
haṃsasya ca varaṃ prādāttoye ratimavāpsyasi ..
varṇataścandraraśmyābho bhaviṣyasi tathaiva ca .. 12 ..
1.181.d:
हंसस्य च वरं प्रादात्तोये रतिमवाप्स्यसि ॥
वर्णतश्चन्द्ररश्म्याभो भविष्यसि तथैव च ॥ 12 ॥
1.181.m: And he granted a boon to the swan: ‘You will find pleasure in the water, / and likewise your colour will resemble the rays of the moon.’

1.181.s:
yamo vāyasarūpeṇa tasyādyajñādapākamat ..
vāyasasya varaṃ prādādamaratvaṃ vinā vadhāt.. 13..
1.181.d:
यमो वायसरूपेण तस्याद्यज्ञादपाकमत् ॥
वायसस्य वरं प्रादादमरत्वं विना वधात्॥ 13॥
1.181.m: Yama slipped away from that sacrifice in the form of a crow; / he granted a boon to the crow: ‘Immortality except by slaughter.

1.181.s:
yuṣmaddattena cānnena ghorā madviṣaye sthitāḥ ..
parāṃ tṛptiṃ gamiṣyanti tadā puṇyena yokṣyase .. 14 ..
1.181.d:
युष्मद्दत्तेन चान्नेन घोरा मद्विषये स्थिताः ॥
परां तृप्तिं गमिष्यन्ति तदा पुण्येन योक्ष्यसे ॥ 14 ॥
1.181.m: And by means of the food offered by you, the terrifying [spirits] stationed in my realm / will attain supreme satisfaction, and you will then be endowed with merit.

1.181.s:
vakṣyadhvaṃ balidātṝṇāṃ digdeśagataceṣṭitaiḥ ..
śubhāśubhaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ tatrātithyaṃ bhaviṣyati ..15..
1.181.d:
वक्ष्यध्वं बलिदातॄणां दिग्देशगतचेष्टितैः ॥
शुभाशुभं मनुष्याणां तत्रातिथ्यं भविष्यति ॥15॥
1.181.m: You will foretell the good and bad fortune of men who offer oblations, / by your movements directed to the quarters and regions; hospitality will be shown to you there.

1.181.s:
vajratuṇḍāśca ye kākā ghorā madviṣaye sthitāḥ ..
balipiṇḍām̐śca dātṝṇāṃ bhaviṣyanti tataḥ śivam .. 16 ..
1.181.d:
वज्रतुण्डाश्च ये काका घोरा मद्विषये स्थिताः ॥
बलिपिण्डाम्̐श्च दातॄणां भविष्यन्ति ततः शिवम् ॥ 16 ॥
1.181.m: And the terrifying crows with diamond beaks that abide in my realm / will [partake of] the oblation-balls of the givers, and good fortune will follow from that.’

1.181.s:
maruttayajñe vitrāsaṃ janayitvā divaukasām ..
babhrāma vasudhāṃ rājā rākṣasānāṃ pratāpavān .. 17 ..
1.181.d:
मरुत्तयज्ञे वित्रासं जनयित्वा दिवौकसाम् ॥
बभ्राम वसुधां राजा राक्षसानां प्रतापवान् ॥ 17 ॥
1.181.m: Having produced terror among the celestials at the sacrifice of Marutta, / the powerful king of the rakshasas roamed over the earth.

1.181.s:
dadarśa sa tadā kanyāṃ tapasyantīṃ mahattapaḥ ..
rūpeṇāpratimāṃ loke yauvane prathame sthitām..18..
1.181.d:
ददर्श स तदा कन्यां तपस्यन्तीं महत्तपः ॥
रूपेणाप्रतिमां लोके यौवने प्रथमे स्थिताम्॥18॥
1.181.m: He then saw a maiden performing severe asceticism, / peerless in beauty in the world, in the first flush of youth.

1.181.s:
daśagrīvaḥ sa papraccha tāṃ kanyāṃ lokasundarīm..
kā tvaṃ kimarthaṃ suśroṇi cāsthitā yauvane tapaḥ..19 ..
1.181.d:
दशग्रीवः स पप्रच्छ तां कन्यां लोकसुन्दरीम्॥
का त्वं किमर्थं सुश्रोणि चास्थिता यौवने तपः॥19 ॥
1.181.m: Daśagrīva questioned that maiden of worldly beauty: / ‘Who are you, and why, O fair-hipped one, have you undertaken asceticism in youth?’

1.181.s:
śrutvā tasya tu sā kanyā satyaṃ vacanamabravīt ..
bṛhaspatisuto vidvānpitā mama kuśadhvajaḥ ..1.221.20..
1.181.d:
श्रुत्वा तस्य तु सा कन्या सत्यं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥
बृहस्पतिसुतो विद्वान्पिता मम कुशध्वजः ॥1.221.20॥
1.181.m: Hearing him, that maiden spoke true words: / ‘The wise Kuśadhvaja, son of Bṛhaspati, is my father.

1.181.s:
vedābhyāsapravṛttasya tasyāhaṃ nṛpabāndhavā..
sutāparā samutpannā tatpatnyā viditā tathā .. 21 ..
1.181.d:
वेदाभ्यासप्रवृत्तस्य तस्याहं नृपबान्धवा॥
सुतापरा समुत्पन्ना तत्पत्न्या विदिता तथा ॥ 21 ॥
1.181.m: Of him engaged in the study of the Vedas, O kin of kings, / I was born as another daughter, likewise acknowledged by his wife,

1.181.s:
nāmnā vedavatītyevaṃ khyātā lokeṣu rākṣasa ..
viṣṇormayeyaṃ dātavyā tasyāsīnme piturmatiḥ .. 22 ..
1.181.d:
नाम्ना वेदवतीत्येवं ख्याता लोकेषु राक्षस ॥
विष्णोर्मयेयं दातव्या तस्यासीन्मे पितुर्मतिः ॥ 22 ॥
1.181.m: known by the name Vedavatī in the worlds, O rakshasa. / “She should be given by me to Viṣṇu”—such was my father’s intention.

1.181.s:
madyācanā nirastena daityanāthena śambhunā ..
pitā mama hato rātrau tamāliṅgya vibhāvasum .. 23 ..
1.181.d:
मद्याचना निरस्तेन दैत्यनाथेन शम्भुना ॥
पिता मम हतो रात्रौ तमालिङ्ग्य विभावसुम् ॥ 23 ॥
1.181.m: Rebuffed in his suit for me, the daitya king Śambhu / killed my father at night; embracing the sacrificial fire,

1.181.s:
praviṣṭā janayitrī me yathāhaṃ vidhṛtā ciram ..
svargasthasya pituḥ kāmaṃ sāhaṃ satyamabhīpsatī .. 24 ..
1.181.d:
प्रविष्टा जनयित्री मे यथाहं विधृता चिरम् ॥
स्वर्गस्थस्य पितुः कामं साहं सत्यमभीप्सती ॥ 24 ॥
1.181.m: my mother entered [the flames] as I was held back for a long time. / Wishing to fulfill the true desire of my father residing in heaven,

1.181.s:
ārādhayāmi tapasā patyarthaṃ madhusūdanam ..
tatastāmabravīdrakṣo mā tvaṃ kleśe matiṃ kṛthāḥ ..25 ..
1.181.d:
आराधयामि तपसा पत्यर्थं मधुसूदनम् ॥
ततस्तामब्रवीद्रक्षो मा त्वं क्लेशे मतिं कृथाः ॥25 ॥
1.181.m: I worship Madhusūdana with asceticism to have him as my husband.’ / Then the rakshasa said to her: ‘Do not set your mind on distress!

1.181.s:
bhavasva me varārohe bhāryā trailokyasundarī ..
rūpasya vayasaścaiva nānurūpaṃ tapastava .. 26 ..
1.181.d:
भवस्व मे वरारोहे भार्या त्रैलोक्यसुन्दरी ॥
रूपस्य वयसश्चैव नानुरूपं तपस्तव ॥ 26 ॥
1.181.m: Become my wife, O woman of lovely hips, beauty of the three worlds! / Your asceticism is not suited to your beauty and youth.

1.181.s:
tvāṃ kṛtvoparato manye rūpaṃ kṛtvā sa viśvakṛt ..
na hi rūpopamā tvanyā tathāsti sadṛśī yataḥ .. 27 ..
1.181.d:
त्वां कृत्वोपरतो मन्ये रूपं कृत्वा स विश्वकृत् ॥
न हि रूपोपमा त्वन्या तथास्ति सदृशी यतः ॥ 27 ॥
1.181.m: I think that the creator of all, having made your form, has ceased; / for there is no other counterpart equal to your beauty.’

1.181.s:
saṃpūrṇakāntimatsaumyaṃ vadanaṃ te varānane ..
sakalaṃkena candreṇa kathamopamyamarhati .. ..28..
1.181.d:
संपूर्णकान्तिमत्सौम्यं वदनं ते वरानने ॥
सकलंकेन चन्द्रेण कथमोपम्यमर्हति ॥ ॥28॥
1.181.m: Your gentle face possessed of full radiance, O fair-faced woman, / how does it deserve comparison with the moon, which bears a blemish?

1.181.s:
bhava bhūṣaṇajātānāṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ tvaṃ śucismite ..
vṛṇuṣva māṃ varārohe patitve varavarṇini .. 29..
1.181.d:
भव भूषणजातानां भूषणं त्वं शुचिस्मिते ॥
वृणुष्व मां वरारोहे पतित्वे वरवर्णिनि ॥ 29॥
1.181.m: Be the ornament of all kinds of ornaments, O woman of pure smiles! / Choose me, O woman of lovely hips, as your husband, O fair-complexioned one!

1.181.s:
ākramyākramya lokasya pradhānā yā mayā hṛtāḥ..
striyaḥ kuruṣva sarvāsāṃ tāsāṃ svāmyamanindite ..1.221.30..
1.181.d:
आक्रम्याक्रम्य लोकस्य प्रधाना या मया हृताः॥
स्त्रियः कुरुष्व सर्वासां तासां स्वाम्यमनिन्दिते ॥1.221.30॥
1.181.m: The foremost women of the world whom I have abducted after repeatedly attacking, / exercise lordship over all of them, O blameless one!

1.181.s:
jaṭāmālājinadharī tvamevaṃ rativardhinī ..
na jāne maṇḍanāṃ prāpya kathaṃ bhīru bhavi ṣyasi .. 31 ..
1.181.d:
जटामालाजिनधरी त्वमेवं रतिवर्धिनी ॥
न जाने मण्डनां प्राप्य कथं भीरु भवि ष्यसि ॥ 31 ॥
1.181.m: Wearing a garland of matted locks and an antelope skin, you increase [my] longing in this way; / I do not know, O timid one, how you will be once you have attained adornments.

1.181.s:
rūpeṇa vayasā lakṣmyā tathaiva guṇasampadā ..
vikrame me varārohe na samo hi janārdanaḥ .. 32 ..
1.181.d:
रूपेण वयसा लक्ष्म्या तथैव गुणसम्पदा ॥
विक्रमे मे वरारोहे न समो हि जनार्दनः ॥ 32 ॥
1.181.m: In beauty, in youth, in fortune, and likewise in wealth of virtues, / indeed Janārdana is not my equal in valour, O woman of lovely hips.

1.181.s:
janma tasya na jānanti parebhyo ye pare janāḥ ..
tena tvamakulīnena kiṅkariṣyasi sundari .. 33 ..
1.181.d:
जन्म तस्य न जानन्ति परेभ्यो ये परे जनाः ॥
तेन त्वमकुलीनेन किङ्करिष्यसि सुन्दरि ॥ 33 ॥
1.181.m: People whose origins are higher than the highest do not know his birth; / with him who has no noble lineage, what will you do, O beautiful woman?

1.181.s:
anindraṃ lokamicchantī surāṇāṃ hitakāmyayā ..
hatā yenānuvṛttena yoṣitkāvyā raṇiḥ purā .. 34 ..
1.181.d:
अनिन्द्रं लोकमिच्छन्ती सुराणां हितकाम्यया ॥
हता येनानुवृत्तेन योषित्काव्या रणिः पुरा ॥ 34 ॥
1.181.m: By him, wishing for the welfare of the gods, longing for a world without Indra, / the woman Kāvī was formerly killed in battle through [mere] conformity [to duty].

1.181.s:
purāṇā ye jagatyasmim̐stebhyaḥ pūrvatarāśca ye ..
tebhyo'pyati purāṇaṃ taṃ bhartāraṃ kathamicchasi .. 35 ..
1.181.d:
पुराणा ये जगत्यस्मिम्̐स्तेभ्यः पूर्वतराश्च ये ॥
तेभ्योऽप्यति पुराणं तं भर्तारं कथमिच्छसि ॥ 35 ॥
1.181.m: Those who are ancient in this world, and those who are even earlier than they— / how do you desire as a husband him who is exceedingly ancient even compared to them?

1.181.s:
brahmaṇo varadānena yastvavadhyo divaukasām ..
te daityanāthāḥ sabalāśchadmanā tena ghātitāḥ .. 36 ..
1.181.d:
ब्रह्मणो वरदानेन यस्त्ववध्यो दिवौकसाम् ॥
ते दैत्यनाथाः सबलाश्छद्मना तेन घातिताः ॥ 36 ॥
1.181.m: By him, through deceit, were slain those lords of Daityas together with their armies, / who were invulnerable to the sky-dwellers by the boon of Brahmā.

1.181.s:
tatpratāpa?niviṣṭena cetasā rakṣasāṃ śriyam ..
yo bibhartyapi tāṃ tena kiṃ kariṣyati bhāmini .. 37 ..
1.181.d:
तत्प्रताप?निविष्टेन चेतसा रक्षसां श्रियम् ॥
यो बिभर्त्यपि तां तेन किं करिष्यति भामिनि ॥ 37 ॥
1.181.m: He who maintains the fortune of the Rākṣasas with a mind focused on its splendour— / what will he do with that [fortune], O passionate woman?

1.181.s:
vṛddhebhyo na śrutaṃ tasya tvayā rūpamanindite ..
viditaṃ sarvalokānāṃ viśvarūpadharastvasau .. 38 ..
1.181.d:
वृद्धेभ्यो न श्रुतं तस्य त्वया रूपमनिन्दिते ॥
विदितं सर्वलोकानां विश्वरूपधरस्त्वसौ ॥ 38 ॥
1.181.m: Have you not heard from the elders of his form, O blameless one? / It is known to all the worlds; indeed, he bears a universal form.

1.181.s:
śeṣāhibhogaparyaṅke tena tvaṃ śayitā saha ..
saviṣairbhoganiśvāsaiḥ parāṃ glānimupaiṣyasi .. 31...
1.181.d:
शेषाहिभोगपर्यङ्के तेन त्वं शयिता सह ॥
सविषैर्भोगनिश्वासैः परां ग्लानिमुपैष्यसि ॥ 31॥।
1.181.m: Sleeping with him upon the couch of the coils of the serpent Śeṣa, / you will come to extreme exhaustion through the venomous exhalations of the coils.

1.181.s:
kaṇṭhagraheṇa nihatau yena tau madhukaiṭabhau ..
kathaṃ kaṇṭhagrahaṃ tasya samupaiṣyasi sundari .. 1.221.40 ..
1.181.d:
कण्ठग्रहेण निहतौ येन तौ मधुकैटभौ ॥
कथं कण्ठग्रहं तस्य समुपैष्यसि सुन्दरि ॥ 1.221.40 ॥
1.181.m: By him those two, Madhu and Kaiṭabha, were slain by seizing their throats; / how will you approach his embrace of your throat, O beautiful woman?

1.181.s:
hiraṇyakaśipuryena nakhairutkāntajīvitaḥ ..
kathaṃ ratyantare tasya nakhāghātaṃ sahiṣyasi .. 41 ..
1.181.d:
हिरण्यकशिपुर्येन नखैरुत्कान्तजीवितः ॥
कथं रत्यन्तरे तस्य नखाघातं सहिष्यसि ॥ 41 ॥
1.181.m: By whom Hiraṇyakaśipu was deprived of life with claws; / how will you endure his claw-wounds in the midst of lovemaking?

1.181.s:
tasmādbhāvaṃ samutsṛjya cārugātri janārdane ..
bhajasva bhajamānaṃ māṃ ciraṃ prītimavāpnuhi .. 42 .. ..
1.181.d:
तस्माद्भावं समुत्सृज्य चारुगात्रि जनार्दने ॥
भजस्व भजमानं मां चिरं प्रीतिमवाप्नुहि ॥ 42 ॥ ॥
1.181.m: Therefore, abandoning [your] affection for Janārdana, O woman of lovely limbs, / devote yourself to me who am devoted to you, and obtain delight for a long time!

1.181.s:
vedavatyuvāca ..
guṇā eva sureśasya doṣāste rajanīcara ..
jagatprakāśakā bhānorulūkasyeva raśmayaḥ .. 43 ..
1.181.d:
वेदवत्युवाच ॥
गुणा एव सुरेशस्य दोषास्ते रजनीचर ॥
जगत्प्रकाशका भानोरुलूकस्येव रश्मयः ॥ 43 ॥
1.181.m: Vedavatī said: / The very virtues of the lord of the gods appear as faults to you, O night-wanderer, / just as the rays of the sun, which illuminate the world, [are dark] to an owl.

1.181.s:
kiṃ tvayā saha vādena varaṇīyaḥ sa me prabhuḥ ..
yādṛśastādṛśo vāpi patitve rajanīcara .. 44 ..
1.181.d:
किं त्वया सह वादेन वरणीयः स मे प्रभुः ॥
यादृशस्तादृशो वापि पतित्वे रजनीचर ॥ 44 ॥
1.181.m: What is the use of disputing with you? He is my lord to be chosen, / of whatever nature he may be, as my husband, O night-wanderer.

1.181.s:
iti vedavatīvākyaṃ śrutvā kopasamanvitaḥ ..
kāmena rākṣasendrantāṃ keśapāśe parāmṛśata .. 45 ..
1.181.d:
इति वेदवतीवाक्यं श्रुत्वा कोपसमन्वितः ॥
कामेन राक्षसेन्द्रन्तां केशपाशे परामृशत ॥ 45 ॥
1.181.m: Having heard this speech of Vedavatī, filled with rage / and overcome by desire, the lord of the Rākṣasas touched her braid of hair.

1.181.s:
tvayā saṃdharṣitā pāpa pravekṣyāmi hutāśanam ..
ayonijā bhaviṣyāmi vadhārthaṃ na tathā tava .. 45 ..
1.181.d:
त्वया संधर्षिता पाप प्रवेक्ष्यामि हुताशनम् ॥
अयोनिजा भविष्यामि वधार्थं न तथा तव ॥ 45 ॥
1.181.m: "Assaulted by you, O wicked one, I shall enter the sacrificial fire; / I shall be born without a womb for your destruction, not otherwise."

1.181.s:
evamuktvā citāṃ kṛtvā praviṣṭā jātavedasam..
bhūya sītā samutpannā janakasya mahātmanaḥ .. 47 ..
1.181.d:
एवमुक्त्वा चितां कृत्वा प्रविष्टा जातवेदसम्॥
भूय सीता समुत्पन्ना जनकस्य महात्मनः ॥ 47 ॥
1.181.m: Having spoken thus and constructed a funeral pyre, she entered the fire; / she was born again as Sītā, [daughter] of the great-souled Janaka,

1.181.s:
ayonijā mahābhāgā karṣato yajñamedinīm ..
bhartāraṃ tapasā viṣṇuṃ rāmaṃ labdhavatī yathā .. 48 ..
1.181.d:
अयोनिजा महाभागा कर्षतो यज्ञमेदिनीम् ॥
भर्तारं तपसा विष्णुं रामं लब्धवती यथा ॥ 48 ॥
1.181.m: not born from a womb, highly fortunate, as he was ploughing the sacrificial ground; / as one who attained Viṣṇu, Rāma, as her husband by means of austerity,

1.181.s:
yasyā arthe sa rāmeṇa daśagrīvo hato raṇe ..
lokāpavādabhītena daśagrīvagṛhoṣitā .. 49 ..
1.181.d:
यस्या अर्थे स रामेण दशग्रीवो हतो रणे ॥
लोकापवादभीतेन दशग्रीवगृहोषिता ॥ 49 ॥
1.181.m: for whose sake the ten-necked [Rāvaṇa] was slain in battle by Rāma. / Because she had dwelt in the house of the ten-necked one, frightened of public slander,

1.181.s:
ataḥ patnī parityaktā sītā bhūyo janeśvara ..
vālmīkerāśrame sā tu prasūtā dārakadvayam .. 1.221.50 ..
1.181.d:
अतः पत्नी परित्यक्ता सीता भूयो जनेश्वर ॥
वाल्मीकेराश्रमे सा तु प्रसूता दारकद्वयम् ॥ 1.221.50 ॥
1.181.m: his wife Sītā was subsequently abandoned, O lord of men. / But in the hermitage of Vālmīki she gave birth to a pair of sons,

1.181.s:
kuśaṃ lavaṃ ca vikrāntau yayoḥ sarvāḥ kriyāḥ kṛtāḥ ..
vālmīkinā mahābhāgau vedamadhyāpitā yathā .. 51 ..
1.181.d:
कुशं लवं च विक्रान्तौ ययोः सर्वाः क्रियाः कृताः ॥
वाल्मीकिना महाभागौ वेदमध्यापिता यथा ॥ 51 ॥
1.181.m: Kuśa and Lava, both valiant, for whom all sacraments were performed / by Vālmīki, both highly fortunate, and whom he taught the Veda.

1.181.s:
prakarṣaṃ ca dhanurvede pāraṃ nītā tu tau śiśū ..
vālmīkinā tathā kṛtvā rāmasya caritaṃ śubhama .. 52 ..
1.181.d:
प्रकर्षं च धनुर्वेदे पारं नीता तु तौ शिशू ॥
वाल्मीकिना तथा कृत्वा रामस्य चरितं शुभम ॥ 52 ॥
1.181.m: Both children were brought to excellence and mastery in the science of archery; / and having composed the auspicious life-story of Rāma,

1.181.s:
adhyāpito viśālākṣau dārakau priyadarśanau ..
agāyatāṃ tatastau tu rāmayaje kumāgkā .. 53 ..
1.181.d:
अध्यापितो विशालाक्षौ दारकौ प्रियदर्शनौ ॥
अगायतां ततस्तौ तु रामयजे कुमाग्का ॥ 53 ॥
1.181.m: Vālmīki taught the two large-eyed, handsome boys. / Then those two youths sang at the sacrifice of Rāma

1.181.s:
rāmasya caritaṃ kṛtsnaṃ rāmasya purataḥ sthitau ..
tasmātkāvyāttu vijñāya putrau tau priyadarśanau .. 54 ..
1.181.d:
रामस्य चरितं कृत्स्नं रामस्य पुरतः स्थितौ ॥
तस्मात्काव्यात्तु विज्ञाय पुत्रौ तौ प्रियदर्शनौ ॥ 54 ॥
1.181.m: the entire life-story of Rāma, standing in the presence of Rāma. / Having recognised from that poem those two handsome boys as his sons,

1.181.s:
yajñe tāṃ ca tathābhūtāmānayāmāma satvaraḥ ..
uvāca ca varārohāṃ pratyayaṃ kuru me śubhe .. 55 ..
1.181.d:
यज्ञे तां च तथाभूतामानयामाम सत्वरः ॥
उवाच च वरारोहां प्रत्ययं कुरु मे शुभे ॥ 55 ॥
1.181.m: he quickly had her brought to the sacrifice in that condition, / and said to that woman of lovely hips: "Give me proof, O auspicious one!"

1.181.s:
rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā sītā vacanamabravīta ..
yathā'haṃ rāghavādanyaṃ manasāpi na kāmaye .. 56 ..
1.181.d:
रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा सीता वचनमब्रवीत ॥
यथाऽहं राघवादन्यं मनसापि न कामये ॥ 56 ॥
1.181.m: Having heard the words of Rāma, Sītā spoke these words: / "As I do not desire anyone other than the descendant of Raghu even in my mind,

1.181.s:
tena satyena me devī vivaraṃ saṃprayacchatu ..
etasminneva kāle tu bhuvaṃ bhittvā samutthitam .. 57 ..
1.181.d:
तेन सत्येन मे देवी विवरं संप्रयच्छतु ॥
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु भुवं भित्त्वा समुत्थितम् ॥ 57 ॥
1.181.m: by that truth let the goddess [Earth] grant me an opening." / At that very time, bursting through the earth, there arose

1.181.s:
dhṛtaṃ siṃhāsanaṃ nāgaistatraināmupaveśayat ..
svayaṃ vasumatī devī pātālaṃ sā tato gatā .. 58 ..
1.181.d:
धृतं सिंहासनं नागैस्तत्रैनामुपवेशयत् ॥
स्वयं वसुमती देवी पातालं सा ततो गता ॥ 58 ॥
1.181.m: a lion-throne held up by serpent-deities; on it the goddess Vasumatī herself / seated her, and she then went to the netherworld,

1.181.s:
avicchinnena patatā puṣpavarṇena pārthiva ..
tasyāṃ bhūmipraviṣṭāyāṃ rāghavaṃ krodhasaṃyutam .. 59 ..
1.181.d:
अविच्छिन्नेन पतता पुष्पवर्णेन पार्थिव ॥
तस्यां भूमिप्रविष्टायां राघवं क्रोधसंयुतम् ॥ 59 ॥
1.181.m: amidst a continuous falling rain of flowers, O king. / When she had entered the earth, the descendant of Raghu, filled with anger,

1.181.s:
sāntvayāmāsa vai brahmā sarvalokanamasrkṛtaḥ ..
rāmo'pi kṛtvā sauvarṇīṃ sītāṃ patnīṃ yaśasvinīm .. 1.221.60 ..
1.181.d:
सान्त्वयामास वै ब्रह्मा सर्वलोकनमस्र्कृतः ॥
रामोऽपि कृत्वा सौवर्णीं सीतां पत्नीं यशस्विनीम् ॥ 1.221.60 ॥
1.181.m: was consoled by Brahmā, who is revered by all the worlds. / Rāma, too, having made a golden [image of] Sītā, his renowned wife,

1.181.s:
īje yajñairbahuvidhaiḥ saha bhātṛbhiracyutaḥ ..
nāpadbhayaṃ na vidhavā na ca vyālakṛtaṃ bhayama .. 61 ..
1.181.d:
ईजे यज्ञैर्बहुविधैः सह भातृभिरच्युतः ॥
नापद्भयं न विधवा न च व्यालकृतं भयम ॥ 61 ॥
1.181.m: the imperishable one sacrificed with various sacrifices along with his brothers. / There was no fear of calamity, no widow, and no fear caused by wild beasts,

1.181.s:
na ca vyādhikṛtaṃ kiñcidrāme rājyaṃ praśāsati ..
ājānubāhurdharmātmā siṃhaskandho nareśvaraḥ .. 62 ..
1.181.d:
न च व्याधिकृतं किञ्चिद्रामे राज्यं प्रशासति ॥
आजानुबाहुर्धर्मात्मा सिंहस्कन्धो नरेश्वरः ॥ 62 ॥
1.181.m: nor was there anything caused by disease, while Rāma was ruling the kingdom. / His arms reaching to his knees, righteous in soul, lion-shouldered, a lord of men,

1.181.s:
pṛthvī sasāgarāṃ rāmo dharmeṇānvaśipatprabhuḥ ..
devāśca ṛṣayaścaiva gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ .. 63 ..
1.181.d:
पृथ्वी ससागरां रामो धर्मेणान्वशिपत्प्रभुः ॥
देवाश्च ऋषयश्चैव गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणाः ॥ 63 ॥
1.181.m: the lord Rāma governed the earth along with the oceans in accordance with dharma. / And the gods and the ṛṣis, and the hosts of Gandharvas and Apsarases,

1.181.s:
yakṣāśca bhūtāni tathā kinnarāścaiva rākṣasāḥ ..
mānuṣyāṇāṃ darśanaṃ te saumyāḥ santo yayussadā .. 64 ..
1.181.d:
यक्षाश्च भूतानि तथा किन्नराश्चैव राक्षसाः ॥
मानुष्याणां दर्शनं ते सौम्याः सन्तो ययुस्सदा ॥ 64 ॥
1.181.m: the Yakṣas, spirits, and likewise the Kinnaras and Rākṣasas, / being gentle, continually came into the sight of humans.

1.181.s:
yadarthameṣā carati gāthā loke purātanī ..
ājānubāhuḥ siṃhāsyaḥ kambugrīvo mahābalaḥ .. 65 ..
1.181.d:
यदर्थमेषा चरति गाथा लोके पुरातनी ॥
आजानुबाहुः सिंहास्यः कम्बुग्रीवो महाबलः ॥ 65 ॥
1.181.m: For which reason this ancient verse circulates in the world: / "Arms reaching to his knees, lion-faced, conch-necked, of great strength,

1.181.s:
sarvabhūtaśaraṇyaśca viṣṇurmānuṣyatāṃ gataḥ ..
satyavānanṛśaṃsaśca jāto bhaktajanapriyaḥ .. 66 ..
1.181.d:
सर्वभूतशरण्यश्च विष्णुर्मानुष्यतां गतः ॥
सत्यवाननृशंसश्च जातो भक्तजनप्रियः ॥ 66 ॥
1.181.m: a refuge for all beings, Viṣṇu attained human state; / truthful, not cruel, he was born dear to his devoted people,

1.181.s:
dhṛtiyukto dayāśīlo dharmayukto jitendriyaḥ ..
mitavāgapi kāryeṣu vaktā vācaspateḥ samaḥ .. 67 ..
1.181.d:
धृतियुक्तो दयाशीलो धर्मयुक्तो जितेन्द्रियः ॥
मितवागपि कार्येषु वक्ता वाचस्पतेः समः ॥ 67 ॥
1.181.m: endowed with fortitude, compassionate in nature, endowed with dharma, self-controlled, / of measured speech, yet in affairs an orator equal to Bṛhaspati,

1.181.s:
vīryavānna ca vīryeṇa mahatā tena vismitaḥ ..
tejasā bhāskagsamaḥ kṣamayā pṛthivīsamaḥ .. 68 ..
1.181.d:
वीर्यवान्न च वीर्येण महता तेन विस्मितः ॥
तेजसा भास्कग्समः क्षमया पृथिवीसमः ॥ 68 ॥
1.181.m: heroic, yet not astonished at that great heroism, / equal to the sun in splendour, equal to the earth in patience,

1.181.s:
maheśvarasamaḥ krodhe nītāvuśanasā samaḥ ..
evaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu guṇairdāśarathirbabhau .. 69 ..
1.181.d:
महेश्वरसमः क्रोधे नीतावुशनसा समः ॥
एवं सर्वेषु भूतेषु गुणैर्दाशरथिर्बभौ ॥ 69 ॥
1.181.m: equal to Maheśvara in anger, equal to Uśanas in statecraft." / Thus among all beings the son of Daśaratha shone with virtues.

1.181.s:
varṇānāmāśramāṇāṃ ca na sāṅkaryaṃ nṛpottame ..
dharmiṣṭhāśca janāḥ sarve rāme rājyaṃ praśāsati .. 1.221.70 ..
1.181.d:
वर्णानामाश्रमाणां च न साङ्कर्यं नृपोत्तमे ॥
धर्मिष्ठाश्च जनाः सर्वे रामे राज्यं प्रशासति ॥ 1.221.70 ॥
1.181.m: There was no intermixture of the social classes and the stages of life under that foremost of kings; / and all the people were exceedingly righteous while Rāma was ruling the kingdom.

1.181.s:
nirdasyurabhavalloko nānarthaḥ kiñcidaspṛśata ..
nākālavarṣī parjanyaḥ sarvasasyadharā dharā ..
janānurāgaśca mahānrāmasya viditātmanaḥ ..71..
1.181.d:
निर्दस्युरभवल्लोको नानर्थः किञ्चिदस्पृशत ॥
नाकालवर्षी पर्जन्यः सर्वसस्यधरा धरा ॥
जनानुरागश्च महान्रामस्य विदितात्मनः ॥71॥
1.181.m: The world was free of thieves, no misfortune touched anyone, / Parjanya did not rain out of season, the earth bore all crops, / and great was the affection of the people for Rāma of realised soul.

1.181.s:
na te kṣamaṃ tena narendracandra vairaṃ mahātmā sa tu lokapūjyaḥ ..
tasyāstravegasya raṇe ca vegaṃ soḍhuṃ na śaktāstridaśāḥ saśakrāḥ ..72 ..
1.222
śailūṣa uvāca ..
vahnipraviṣṭāṃ saṃprekṣya tadā vedavatīṃ dvija ..
kiṃ cakāra mahātejā daśagrīvaḥ pratāpavān..1..
nāḍāyana uvāca..
jagāma sa tadā laṅkāṃ pūjyamāno niśācaraiḥ ..
tatrasthaṃ prerayāmāsa dūtaṃ dhanapatiḥ svayam .. 2 ..
akāryādvinivartasva suraiste cintyate vadhaḥ ..
dūtasya vacanaṃ śrutvā dūtaṃ hatvā niśācaraḥ ..3..
gatvā vijigye dhanadaṃ vijahārā'sya puṣpakam ..
puṣpakeṇa vimānena kailāsaṃ sa tadā yayau .. 4 ..
puṣpakasya gatiṃ ruddhāṃ tatra vīkṣya niśācaraḥ ..
dadarśa śailaśṛṅgasthaṃ nandinaṃ vānarākṛtim .. 5 ..
taṃ dṛṣṭvā mumuce hāsaṃ nandī taṃ śaptavāṃstataḥ ..
girāvasmindaśagrīva svayaṃ krīḍati śaṅkaraḥ ..6..
1.181.d:
न ते क्षमं तेन नरेन्द्रचन्द्र वैरं महात्मा स तु लोकपूज्यः ॥
तस्यास्त्रवेगस्य रणे च वेगं सोढुं न शक्तास्त्रिदशाः सशक्राः ॥72 ॥
1.222
शैलूष उवाच ॥
वह्निप्रविष्टां संप्रेक्ष्य तदा वेदवतीं द्विज ॥
किं चकार महातेजा दशग्रीवः प्रतापवान्॥1॥
नाडायन उवाच॥
जगाम स तदा लङ्कां पूज्यमानो निशाचरैः ॥
तत्रस्थं प्रेरयामास दूतं धनपतिः स्वयम् ॥ 2 ॥
अकार्याद्विनिवर्तस्व सुरैस्ते चिन्त्यते वधः ॥
दूतस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा दूतं हत्वा निशाचरः ॥3॥
गत्वा विजिग्ये धनदं विजहाराऽस्य पुष्पकम् ॥
पुष्पकेण विमानेन कैलासं स तदा ययौ ॥ 4 ॥
पुष्पकस्य गतिं रुद्धां तत्र वीक्ष्य निशाचरः ॥
ददर्श शैलशृङ्गस्थं नन्दिनं वानराकृतिम् ॥ 5 ॥
तं दृष्ट्वा मुमुचे हासं नन्दी तं शप्तवांस्ततः ॥
गिरावस्मिन्दशग्रीव स्वयं क्रीडति शङ्करः ॥6॥
1.181.m:
Enmity with him is not fitting for you, O moon among kings; for that great-souled one is revered by the worlds. / In battle, not even the thirty [gods] with Śakra are able to withstand the fury of the force of his weapons.
1.222
Śailūṣa said:
Seeing Vedavatī entering the fire at that time, O twice-born,
what did the ten-necked, glorious, majestic [Rāvaṇa] do?
Nāḍāyana said:
He then went to Laṅkā, honoured by the night-wanderers.
The Lord of Wealth himself dispatched a messenger to him residing there:
"Turn back from what should not be done! Your slaying is being plotted by the gods."
Having heard the messenger's words and having killed the messenger, the night-wanderer,
having gone, conquered the Giver of Wealth and carried off his Puṣpaka [chariot].
In that Puṣpaka aerial chariot he then went to Kailāsa.
Seeing the passage of the Puṣpaka blocked there, the night-wanderer
saw Nandin, who had the form of a monkey, stationed on the peak of the mountain.
Having seen him, he burst into laughter. Thereupon Nandin cursed him:
"On this mountain, O ten-necked one, Śaṅkara himself sports.

1.181.s:
vimānena yadā tasya samīpamupayāsyasi..
karoṣi cāvahāsyaṃ māṃ tasmācchapsyāmyahaṃ tava .. 7 ..
madvaktrasadṛśā ghorāḥ pulahasya prajāpateḥ ..
utpatsyanti kule bhīmāḥ kṣayārthaṃ vānarāstava .. 8 ..
śrutvainaṃ nandino vākyaṃ sakailāsaṃ trilocanam ..
netukāmastadā laṅkāṃ bhujāñcikṣepa parvate .. 9 ..
paulastyabhujasaṃkṣubdhakailāsacalitāsanā ..
jagrāha nirbharaṃ kaṇṭhe tadomā tripurāntakam .. 1.222.10 ..
tato garjanmahādevo devānāṃ pravaro haraḥ ..
pādāṅguṣṭhena taṃ śailaṃ pīḍayāmāsa līlayā .. 11 ..
rakṣasā tena roṣācca bhujānāṃ rujayā tathā ..
mukto virāvaḥ sumahāṃstrailokyaṃ yena rāvitam .. 12 ..
menire vaktraniṣpeṣaṃ tasyāmātyā yugakṣayam ..
āsanebhyaḥ pracalitā devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ .. 13 ..
tena śabdena vitrastā sutarāṃ parvatātmajā ..
harasyāliṅganaṃ cakre bhayalolekṣaṇā bhṛśam .. 14 ..
1.181.d:
विमानेन यदा तस्य समीपमुपयास्यसि॥
करोषि चावहास्यं मां तस्माच्छप्स्याम्यहं तव ॥ 7 ॥
मद्वक्त्रसदृशा घोराः पुलहस्य प्रजापतेः ॥
उत्पत्स्यन्ति कुले भीमाः क्षयार्थं वानरास्तव ॥ 8 ॥
श्रुत्वैनं नन्दिनो वाक्यं सकैलासं त्रिलोचनम् ॥
नेतुकामस्तदा लङ्कां भुजाञ्चिक्षेप पर्वते ॥ 9 ॥
पौलस्त्यभुजसंक्षुब्धकैलासचलितासना ॥
जग्राह निर्भरं कण्ठे तदोमा त्रिपुरान्तकम् ॥ 1.222.10 ॥
ततो गर्जन्महादेवो देवानां प्रवरो हरः ॥
पादाङ्गुष्ठेन तं शैलं पीडयामास लीलया ॥ 11 ॥
रक्षसा तेन रोषाच्च भुजानां रुजया तथा ॥
मुक्तो विरावः सुमहांस्त्रैलोक्यं येन रावितम् ॥ 12 ॥
मेनिरे वक्त्रनिष्पेषं तस्यामात्या युगक्षयम् ॥
आसनेभ्यः प्रचलिता देवाः शक्रपुरोगमाः ॥ 13 ॥
तेन शब्देन वित्रस्ता सुतरां पर्वतात्मजा ॥
हरस्यालिङ्गनं चक्रे भयलोलेक्षणा भृशम् ॥ 14 ॥
1.181.m:
Since you approach his presence with an aerial chariot
and mock me, therefore I shall curse you:
Ferocious monkeys resembling my face, terrible [and born] in the lineage
of the progenitor Pulaha, will arise for your destruction."
Hearing these words of Nandin, and wishing then to carry off
[mount] Kailāsa together with the Three-Eyed [Śiva] to Laṅkā, he thrust his arms under the mountain.
Her seat shaken on Kailāsa as it was agitated by the arms of Pulastya's descendant,
Umā then seized the Destroyer of Tripura tightly by the neck.
Then roaring, Mahādeva, Hara, the foremost of the gods,
pressed down that mountain with his big toe in sport.
By that rākṣasa, out of rage and also out of the agony in his arms,
a tremendous cry was let out, by which the three worlds were made to scream.
His ministers thought the gnashing of his mouths to be the destruction of the world-age.
The gods headed by Śakra were shaken from their seats.
Terrified exceedingly by that sound, the daughter of the mountain,
her eyes restless with fear, embraced Hara intensely.

1.181.d:
अकृत्रिमालिङ्गनजां प्रीतिं प्राप्य तदा हरः ॥
मुक्त्वा चास्य भुजान्राजन्प्राह वाक्यं दशाननम् ॥ 15 ॥
प्रीतोऽस्मि तव वीर्यैश्च शौण्डीर्यैश्च दशानन ॥
यस्मादराक्षसो रावस्त्वया मुक्तो भयङ्करः ॥ 16॥
तस्मात्त्वं रावणो नाम भविष्यसि जगत्त्रये ॥
ततः प्रभृति राजेन्द्र रावणो लोकरावणः ॥ 17 ॥
शातकुम्भमयं लिङ्गं देवदेवस्य शूलिनः ॥
सम्पूजयति राजेन्द्र नित्यं श्रद्धासमन्वितः ॥18॥
यत्रयत्र यथा याति तत्रतत्रास्य पार्थिव ॥
सौवर्णं तस्य देवस्य लिङ्गं तदनु नीयते ॥ 19 ॥
ततस्तु रावणो राजा ययौ संयमनीं पुरीम् ॥
युयुधे कालपाशेभ्यो यागैश्च सह मृत्युना ॥1.222.20॥
जित्वा पितृगणांश्चैव मोक्षयित्वा च नारकान् ॥
यमेन युयुधे सार्धं क्रोधाद्वैवस्तस्ततः ॥ 21 ॥
1.181.m:
Attaining then the delight born from her spontaneous embrace,
and releasing his arms, O king, Hara addressed the ten-faced one:
"I am pleased with your valour and your prowess, O ten-faced one!
Because a terrifying cry, not of a rākṣasa, was emitted by you,
therefore you will be known by the name 'Rāvaṇa' in the three worlds."
From then on, O ruler of kings, [he was called] Rāvaṇa, who makes the worlds cry out.
A liṅga made of gold of the god of gods, the bearer of the trident,
he worships, O ruler of kings, always filled with faith.
Wherever and however he goes, O protector of the earth,
the golden liṅga of that god is carried along after him.
Then King Rāvaṇa went to the city of Saṃyamanī.
He fought with Death and with the snares of Time [and Yama's] sacrifices.
Having conquered the hosts of ancestors and freed the inhabitants of hell,
he fought with Yama. Then the son of Vivasvat out of anger,

1.181.d:
हन्तुमिच्छन्महीपाल दण्डास्त्रेण निशाचरम्॥
वारयामास तं ब्रह्मा वाक्यं चेदमुवाच ह ॥ 22 ॥
अमोघस्तव दण्डोयमवध्यश्चैव रावणः ॥
एकस्मिन्नपि निष्क्रान्ते भूयामनृतवागहम् ॥ 23 ॥
पितामहवचः श्रुत्वा देवस्सोऽन्तर्दधे ततः ॥
रावणः सह सैन्येन ययौ कैलासपर्वतम् ॥ 24 ॥
उवास शर्वरीं तत्र योद्धुकामो दिवालयैः ॥
स तु चन्द्रोदये रात्रौ भ्रातृपुत्राभिसारिकाम् ॥ 25 ॥
ददर्श रम्भां राजन्तीं मेघस्येव शतह्रदाम् ॥
अकामां कामसंतप्तो विध्वंस्य सुरयोषितम् ॥ 26 ॥
अद्यप्रभृति मूर्धा ते शतधा तु गमिष्यति ॥
प्रभातसमये गत्वा सुरसद्म स राक्षसः ॥ 27 ॥
मेघनादेन सहितः कुम्भकर्णेन रक्षसा ॥
देवानां कदनं चक्रे तथान्ये राक्षसोत्तमैः ॥ 28 ॥
तस्मिन्रणमुखे घोरो सावित्रेण तदाऽनघ ॥
सुमाली निहतः संख्ये रावणस्यार्भको बलात ॥ 29 ॥
1.181.m:
desiring to slay the night-wanderer with the weapon of the staff, O protector of the earth,
was stopped by Brahmā, who indeed spoke these words:
"Infallible is this staff of yours, and Rāvaṇa cannot be slain.
If even one [of these conditions] were violated, I would become a speaker of falsehood."
Hearing the words of the Grandfather, that god then vanished.
Rāvaṇa, together with his army, went to Mount Kailāsa.
He dwelt there for the night, desiring to fight with the dwellers of heaven.
At moonrise in the night, [the celestial nymph] who was going to an assignation with his brother's son,
he saw—Rambhā, radiant like a streak of lightning in a cloud.
Afflicted by lust, having violated the celestial woman who was unwilling,
[he was cursed by Nalakūbara:] "From this day forth your head will split into a hundred pieces!"
Going at daybreak to the abode of the gods, that rākṣasa,
accompanied by Meghanāda and the rākṣasa Kumbhakarṇa,
wrought the slaughter of the gods, along with other foremost rākṣasas.
In the thick of that battle, the fierce Sumālī, child of Rāvaṇa's [mother's family],
was forcefully struck down then in combat by the son of Savitṛ, O sinless one.

1.181.d:
अजेयान्राक्षसाञ्ज्ञात्वा पुलोमा नाम दानवः ॥
जयन्तमिन्द्रतनयं दौहित्रं स्वं रणाजिरात् ॥ 1.222.30 ॥
रक्षार्थमनयच्छ्रीमान्स्वगृहं वसुधातले ॥
अपश्यमानं पुत्रं स्वं शक्रं विह्वलचेतसम् ॥ 31 ॥
बबन्ध मेघनादस्तु ब्रह्मलव्धवरः शनैः ॥
अनयच्च तथा लङ्कां ततो देवः पितामहः ॥ 32 ॥
गत्वा तं मोचयामास शक्रं त्रिभुवनेश्वरम् ॥
मेघनादस्य चास्त्राणि मायाश्च विविधास्तथा ॥ ॥ 33 ॥
अमरत्वं तदा प्रादाद्वह्निकर्मान्तरं विना ॥
नाम चक्रे तदा चास्य शक्रजित्त्वं भविष्यसि ॥ 34 ॥
मेघनादं सान्त्वयित्वा मोचयित्वा शतक्रतुम् ॥
उवाच भगवान्ब्रह्मा देवं दशशतेक्षणम् ॥ 35 ॥
गौतमस्य प्रिया भार्या मनसा निर्मिता मया ॥
रूपेणाप्रतिमा शक्र त्वया विध्वंसिता यदा ॥ 36 ॥
1.181.m:
Knowing the rākṣasas to be invincible, a dānava named Pulomā
[took] his own grandson Jayanta, Indra's son, from the battlefield,
and, illustrious, led him to his own home on the surface of the earth for his protection.
[Seeing] Śakra bewildered in mind, not seeing his son,
Meghanāda, who had obtained a boon from Brahmā, bound him slowly
and brought him thus to Laṅkā. Then the divine Grandfather,
having gone, released that Śakra, the lord of the three worlds.
And to Meghanāda [he granted] weapons and diverse magical powers,
and then gave him immortality, except in the interval of a fire ritual.
He then gave him a name: "You shall be Śakrajit [Conqueror of Śakra]."
Having consoled Meghanāda and having released the one of a hundred sacrifices,
the blessed Brahmā addressed the god of a thousand eyes:
"When the dear wife of Gautama, fashioned by me through the mind,
incomparable in beauty, O Śakra, was violated by you,

1.181.d:
तदा गौतमशापेन विफलत्वं गतः स्वयम् ॥
देवैः कृतस्त्वं सम्भूय शेपस्तम्भः पुरन्दर ॥ 37 ॥
अहल्या च तदा शप्ता गौतमेन महात्मना ॥
अदृश्या सर्वभूतानां विचरिष्यसि दुःखिता ॥ 38 ॥
परदाररतश्चासौ द्वे पापं समवाप्स्यति ॥
तेन शापेन संयोगा परदारैश्च वासव ॥ 39 ॥
बन्धनं तत्त्वया प्राप्तं तस्य पापस्य कर्मणः ॥
फलात्त्रिभुवनश्रेष्ठ समरेषु पराजयम् ॥ 1.222.40 ॥
तस्माद्धर्मेण धर्मज्ञ त्पालयस्व जगत्त्रयम् ॥
धर्मो धारयते लोकान्यतो धर्मस्ततो जयः ॥ 41 ॥
गते स्वलोकं भुवनप्रधानं पद्मोद्भवे दानवपूगहर्ता ॥
त्रिविष्टपं प्राप्य शशास राज्यं महानुभावस्त्रिदशाधिनाथः ॥ 42 ॥

1.181.m:
then by Gautama's curse you yourself became devoid of testicles.
You were given the testicles of a ram by the assembled gods, O Purandara.
And Ahalyā was then cursed by the great-souled Gautama:
'Invisible to all beings, you shall wander, full of sorrow!'
And he [Gautama proclaimed]: 'He who delights in another's wife will incur two sins.'
By association with that curse and through [violating] another's wife, O Vāsava,
that captivity was incurred by you, and defeat in battles,
as the fruit of that sinful deed, O foremost of the three worlds.
Therefore, O knower of dharma, protect the three worlds with dharma!
Dharma upholds the worlds; where there is dharma, there is victory."
When the lotus-born [Brahmā], foremost in the universe, had gone to his own realm, the destroyer of the Dānava hosts, / the majestic lord of the thirty [gods], reached heaven and ruled the kingdom.
1.223 / Śailūṣa said: / I wish to hear accurately of the conquest of Pātāla by that great-souled Rāvaṇa, / for I have great curiosity about it.

1.181.d:
नाडायन उवाच ॥ ततः स गत्वा पातालं युयुधे दैत्यसत्तमैः ॥
कालखञ्जैर्महाभागैः कालकेयैश्च दारुणैः ॥ 2 ॥
निवात कवचैश्चैव संवत्सरमतन्द्रितः ॥
पतिं शूर्पणखायास्तु विद्युज्जिह्वं तु दानवम् ॥ 3 ॥
अजावक्त्रवतस्तत्र जघान रणगर्वितम् ॥
तत्रागम्य तदा ब्रह्मा निवातकवचैः सह ॥ 4 ॥
चकार सख्यं सर्वात्मा दशग्रीवस्य रक्षसः ॥
ततस्तु युयुधे नागैर्घोररूपैर्विषोल्बणैः ॥ 5 ॥
वशी कृत्त्वा ततो नागान्वरुणस्य पुरं ययौ ॥
ब्रह्मलोकगते राजन्वरुणे सुमहात्मनि ॥ 6 ॥
पुष्करः प्रददौ युद्धं रावणस्य दुरात्मनः ॥
वरुणस्य सुतः श्रीमाञ्जामाता बलिनस्तथा ॥ 7 ॥
सोमपुत्र्या महाराज ज्योत्स्नया यः स्वयं वृतः ॥
अर्थशास्त्रं विजानाति यः समग्रं महायशाः ॥ 8 ॥
1.181.m:
Nāḍāyana said: / Then, having gone to Pātāla, he fought with the foremost Daityas, / with the illustrious Kālakhañjas and the cruel Kālakeyas,
and untiringly for a year with the Nivātakavacas. / Moreover, the Dānava Vidyujjihva, husband of Śūrpaṇakhā,
who had a goat's face, he slew there as he boasted in battle. / Then Brahmā, having arrived there along with the Nivātakavacas,
the Self of all made friendship for the ten-necked rākṣasa. / Then he fought with the nāgas of terrible form, violent with poison.
Having subdued the nāgas, he then went to the city of Varuṇa. / When the great-souled Varuṇa had gone to the world of Brahmā, O king,
Puṣkara gave battle to the wicked Rāvaṇa— / the glorious son of Varuṇa, and likewise the son-in-law of Bali,
who was chosen in svayaṃvara by the moon's daughter Jyotsnā, O great king, / who fully knew the Arthaśāstra, the renowned one,

the son of Viśravas returned again with his forces to the world of mortals. / Having gone thence to Kiṣkindhā, the city protected by the monkeys,

"What business might you have with Vālin? Tell that to me who am asking." / Rāvaṇa said: / "I seek the hospitality of battle from that monkey.

इदानीमेव निहतो दुन्दुभिस्तेन राक्षसः ॥ 16 ॥
प्रविश्य विवरं घोरं मायावी तेन घातितः ॥
बिले प्रविष्टस्य तदा राजन्संवत्सरसं गतम् ॥ 17 ॥
सुग्रीवेण तदा तस्य द्वारं पिहितमात्मना ॥
स तु संवत्सरस्यान्ते हत्वा मायाविनं रणे ॥ 18 ॥
ददर्श राजन्सुग्रीवं किष्किन्धायां तदाऽनुजम् ॥
स्वपत्न्या रुमया सार्धं वालिपत्न्या च तारया॥19॥
क्रीडमानं यथा शक्रं क्रोधस्य वशमन्वगात् ॥
रुमां तारां तथा हृत्वा तेन निर्वासितस्त्वसौ ॥ 1.223.20 ॥
निर्वासिते तु सुग्रीवे पश्चात्ताप समन्वितः ॥
हन्तुकामस्तु सुग्रीवं वाली पर्यचरन्महीम् ॥21॥
तदा वालिभयत्रस्तः सुग्रीवोऽपि पलायितः ॥
न स लेभे सदा त्राणं तदा सस्मार राक्षसम् ॥ 22 ॥

hundreds more powerful in valour and strength than you were slain by him. / Just now the rākṣasa Dundubhi was slain by him;
entering a terrible cave, Māyāvī was killed by him. / When he entered the cave, O king, a year passed.
Its entrance was then blocked by Sugrīva himself. / But at the end of the year, having killed Māyāvī in battle,
he saw Sugrīva, his younger brother, in Kiṣkindhā, O king, / sporting like Śakra together with his own wife Rumā
and Vālin's wife Tārā, and he came under the sway of wrath. / Having taken back Rumā and Tārā, he was exiled by him.
When Sugrīva had been exiled, Vālin, filled with remorse, / yet wishing to slay Sugrīva, wandered over the earth.
Then Sugrīva too, terrified with fear of Vālin, fled; / he found no protection anywhere, and then he remembered the rākṣasa,

राहुर्जगाम शरणं भयाद्भीतं च वासवम् ॥ 29 ॥
1.181.m:
and likewise Mataṅga's curse upon Vālin, O best of kings. / For having slain Dundubhi, Vālin struck him with the big toe of his foot
and hurled the foremost rākṣasa towards Mataṅga's hermitage. / Seeing his hermitage covered with blood,
Mataṅga angrily cursed Vālin: "In this great forest of mine, / the moment he enters, his life shall cease to be."
Knowing Mataṅga's great forest to be inaccessible to Vālin, / Sugrīva resorted to it together with four ministers:
with Nala, O king, Nīla, Tāra, and Hanūmat. / Hanūmat was his minister, fearless even before the gods,
who, as soon as he was born in childhood, seeing the sun, leapt into the sky; / seeking food, and seeing the night-prowling Rāhu beside him,
abandoning the sun, he ran after Rāhu seeking food. / Rāhu fled in terror and sought refuge with Vāsava.

That very powerful child followed right behind him; / he then saw Śakra's huge-bodied tusker.
Seeking food, he rushed towards that excellent elephant along with Śakra. / Thereupon the lord of the gods quickly struck him with the thunderbolt.
By that strike of the thunderbolt his left jaw was broken; / therefore the Grandfather gave him the name 'Hanumān.'
And having appeased Vāyu, who was enraged with the worlds, the Grandfather / gratified the very powerful Hanumān with a boon.
Together with all the hosts of gods, wishing well to the worlds, / freedom from old age and death, and invincibility in battle
all the deities granted him, and incomparable strength as well. / By the blessed, great-souled Sun himself...

1.181.m:
Śaṅkara said: / I bow to the long-armed one, the god of gods, the lord of Gaṇas, / who has an elephant's face, a huge body, and is covered with a tiger skin garment,
resembling the rays of the moon, with a radiant face and beautiful tusks, / the subduer of obstacles for his devotees, the foremost of gods, the son of Pārvatī,
bearing an axe, the heroic one adorned with a rosary, / benevolent to brahmins, bestower of boons, gentle, the mighty lord of obstacles,
with a plump face, a hanging belly, his stomach encircled by heavy necklaces, / who has chosen the eighth, the fourth, and the fourteenth [lunar days],
whom people in the world worship with gruel, utklopikā pastries, sweetmeat cakes, / and boiled rice, with incenses, garlands, and ointments.
And through recitations of blessings, there is nothing in this world hard for them to attain. / One who desires a son obtains sons; one who desires wealth obtains supreme wealth;
one who is sick attains health; one who is bound is freed from bondage. / Having fully worshipped you, who grant boons and assume shapes at will,
